OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” represents the workmen as a whole. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Tell Hilkiah to give the money to the workmen” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: no accounting was required for the money that was given to them
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the workmen who were in charge did not have to report how they used the money that the temple guards gave them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: given it into the hand of the workmen
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” represents the workmen as a whole. Alternate translation: “given it to the workmen” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: had heard the words of the law
OccurrenceNote: Here “words” represents the message of the law. Alternate translation: “had heard the laws that were written in the book” or “had heard the laws that were written in the scroll” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the words of this book that has been found
OccurrenceNote: Here “words” represents the laws. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the laws in this book that Hilkiah has found” (See:[[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: For great is the anger of Yahweh that has been kindled against us
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s anger is spoken of as if it were a fire that was lit. Alternate translation: “For Yahweh is very angry with us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: all that was written concerning us
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the law that was given to Israel. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “all that Moses wrote in the law that we should do” or “all the laws that God gave through Moses to the people of Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter
OccurrenceNote: Here “second quarter” refers to the new part of the city that was built on the north side of Jerusalem. Also, “second” is the ordinal form of 2. Alternate translation: “she lived in Jerusalem in the new part of the city” or “she lived in the new part of Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-ordinal]])

GLQuote: I will bring disaster to this place and to its inhabitants
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh causing terrible things to happen is spoken of as if disaster were an object that he could bring to a place. Alternate translation: “I will cause terrible things to happen to this place and to those who live there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: to this place
OccurrenceNote: “to Jerusalem.” This refers to the city of Jerusalem which represents the whole land of Judah. Alternate translation: “to Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: my anger has been kindled against this place, and it will not be extinguished
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s anger is spoken of as if it were a fire that was lit. Alternate translation: “my anger against this place is like a fire that cannot be put out” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: this place
OccurrenceNote: Here “place” represents the people who live in Jerusalem and Judah. Alternate translation: “these people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: About the words that you heard
OccurrenceNote: Here “words” represents the message that Huldah just spoke. Alternate translation: “About the message that you heard” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: because your heart was tender
OccurrenceNote: Here “heart” represents a person’s inner being. Feeling sorry is spoken of as if the heart were tender. Alternate translation: “because you felt sorry” or “because you repented” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: that they would become a desolation and a curse
OccurrenceNote: The abstract nouns “desolation” and “curse” can be stated as an adjective and a verb. Alternate translation: “that I would make the land desolate and would curse them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 19:33](../19/33.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: See, I will gather you to your ancestors, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace
OccurrenceNote: Both statements mean basically the same thing. They are polite ways of saying he will die. Alternate translation: “So I will allow you to die and be buried peacefully” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: Your eyes will not see
OccurrenceNote: Here “will not see” represents not experiencing something. Alternate translation: “You will not experience” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Your eyes
OccurrenceNote: Here “eyes” represents the whole person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: the disaster that I will bring upon this place
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh causing terrible things to happen is spoken of as if disaster were an object that Yahweh would bring to a place. Alternate translation: “the terrible things I will cause to happen in this place” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: This is a generalization. Alternate translation: “many other people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: from small to great
OccurrenceNote: This merism includes everyone in between. Alternate translation: “from the least important to the most important” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: that had been found
OccurrenceNote: In [2 Kings 22:8](../22/08.md) it states that Hilkiah found the book. This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “that Hilkiah had found” or “that they had found” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: walk after Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The way a person lives is spoken of as if that person were walking on a path, and “to walk after” someone is a metonym for doing what that other person does or wants others to do. Alternate translation: “live obeying Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: his commandments, his regulations, and his statutes
OccurrenceNote: These words all share similar meanings. Together they emphasize everything that Yahweh had commanded in the law. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: with all his heart and all his soul
OccurrenceNote: The idiom “with all his heart” means “completely” and “with all his soul” means “with all his being.” These two phrases have similar meanings. Alternate translation: “with all his being” or “with all his energy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: that were written in this book
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “that this book contained” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: stand by the covenant
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means to “obey the terms of the covenant.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: He burned … and carried
OccurrenceNote: The word “he” refers to Josiah. He would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “he had them burn them … and carry them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He got rid
OccurrenceNote: The word “He” refers to Josiah. He would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He had them get rid” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He brought out … and burned it … He beat it … and threw
OccurrenceNote: The word “he” refers to Josiah. He would have commanded his workers to do these things. Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He had them bring out … and burn it … He had them beat it … and throw” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He cleared
OccurrenceNote: The word “He” refers to Josiah. He would have commanded his workers to do these things. Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He had them clear” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Josiah brought … and defiled … He destroyed
OccurrenceNote: Josiah would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He commanded them to bring … and to defile … He had them destroy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He took away
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people, perhaps Hilkiah and “the priests under him” ([2 Kings 23:4](../23/04.md)), might have helped Josiah do this. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: had given to the sun
OccurrenceNote: Here “given” represents being dedicated for worship. Alternate translation: “had used to worship the sun” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Josiah the king destroyed … Josiah smashed … and threw
OccurrenceNote: Josiah would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “Josiah the king commanded them to destroy … He had them smash … had them throw” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the kings of Judah had made … Manasseh had made
OccurrenceNote: Manasseh and the kings of Judah probably commanded their workers to make these things. Alternate translation: “the kings of Judah had their workers make … Manasseh had his workers make” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: The king ruined
OccurrenceNote: Josiah would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He had them ruin … He had them break … they filled” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Solomon the king of Israel had built
OccurrenceNote: Solomon would have commanded his workers to do these things. Alternate translation: “Solomon the king of Israel had his workers build” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He broke … he filled
OccurrenceNote: Josiah would have commanded his workers to do these things. It is likely that Hilkiah and the priests who assisted him did these things. Alternate translation: “He had them break … they filled” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: filled those places with the bones of human beings
OccurrenceNote: “covered the ground with human bones so people could not use it as a shrine anymore” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Josiah also completely destroyed … He also burned … and beat … He also burned
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people, perhaps Hilkiah and “the priests under him” ([2 Kings 23:4](../23/04.md)), might have helped Josiah do these things. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Josiah removed … He did
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people, perhaps Hilkiah and “the priests under him” ([2 Kings 23:4](../23/04.md)), might have helped Josiah do these things. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the kings of Israel had made
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people, probably the kings’ workers, might have helped the kings make these things. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He slaughtered … he burned
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people, perhaps Hilkiah and “the priests under him” ([2 Kings 23:4](../23/04.md)), might have helped Josiah do these things. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: he burned human bones on them
OccurrenceNote: You may need to make explicit why he burned the bones. “he burned human bones on them so no one would use them again” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Such a Passover celebration had never been held from the days of
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The descendants of Israel had not celebrated the Passover festival in such a great way in the time of” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: ruled Israel
OccurrenceNote: The name “Israel” is a metonym for “the descendants of Israel.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: this Passover of Yahweh was celebrated
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “the people of Judah celebrated this Passover of Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Yahweh did not turn away from the burning of his fierce anger, which burned against
OccurrenceNote: Fire is a metaphor for anger, and starting a fire is a metaphor for becoming angry. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **anger, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Yahweh did not stop being fierce because he was angry with” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: My name will be there
OccurrenceNote: The name is a metonym for the honor that people should give to the person. Alternate translation: “People should worship me there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: are they not written … Judah?
OccurrenceNote: This can be expressed in active form and assumes that the answer is positive. The question is rhetorical and is used for emphasis. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 8:23](../08/23.md). Alternate translation: “you can find them … Judah.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The sight of Yahweh represents Yahweh’s judgment or evaluation. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 3:2](../03/02.md). Alternate translation: “what was evil in Yahweh’s judgment” or “what Yahweh considers to be evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: put him in chains
OccurrenceNote: Being put “in chains” represents being captured and imprisoned. Alternate translation: “put him in prison” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: did what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The sight of Yahweh represents Yahweh’s judgment or evaluation. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 3:2](../03/02.md). Alternate translation: “what was evil in Yahweh’s judgment” or “what Yahweh considers to be evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: attacked Judah
OccurrenceNote: You may need to make explicit what happened after Nebuchadnezzar attacked Judah. Alternate translation: “attacked and defeated Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: This was in conformity with the word of Yahweh that had been spoken through his servants the prophets
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “This was according to the word of Yahweh that his servants the prophets had spoken” or “This was exactly what Yahweh had told his servants the prophets to say would happen” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: at the mouth of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Here “mouth” represents Yahweh’s command. Alternate translation: “as Yahweh had commanded” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: innocent blood that he shed
OccurrenceNote: Blood is a metonym for innocent life, and shedding blood is a metonym for killing innocent people. Alternate translation: “innocent people whom he killed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood
OccurrenceNote: Blood is a metonym for innocent life, and shedding blood is a metonym for killing innocent people. Alternate translation: “he killed many innocent people in Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: are they not written … Judah?
OccurrenceNote: This is written as a rhetorical question because at the time this was written people were already aware of this information. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. It can be translated in active form. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 8:23](../08/23.md). Alternate translation: “they are indeed written … Judah.” or “you can find them … Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: slept with his ancestors
OccurrenceNote: Sleeping is a euphemism for dying. Alternate translation: “died and was buried along with his ancestors” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The sight of Yahweh represents Yahweh’s judgment or evaluation. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 3:2](../03/02.md). Alternate translation: “what was evil in Yahweh’s judgment” or “what Yahweh considers to be evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he did all that his father had done
OccurrenceNote: Here “all” is a generalization. It means he did the same sinful things as his father. Alternate translation: “he committed the same kinds of sins his father had committed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, his mother, his servants, his princes, and his officers
OccurrenceNote: You may need to make explicit why Jehoiachin went out to meet Nebuchadnezzar. Alternate translation: “Jehoiachin the king of Judah, with his mother, his servants, his princes, and his officers, went out to where the king of Babylon was, to surrender to him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Solomon king of Israel had made
OccurrenceNote: You might want to translate this so the reader understands that Solomon might have had others help him do this. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He took into exile all Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: Here “Jerusalem” is a metonym for the people who lived there. And, “all” is a generalization. It means all the most important people Alternate translation: “Nebuchadnezzar took all the important people away from Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: No one was left except the poorest people in the land
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated as a positive statement. Alternate translation: “Only the poorest people in the land still lived there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublenegatives]])

GLQuote: what was evil in the sight of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The sight of Yahweh represents Yahweh’s judgment or evaluation. See how you translated this in [2 Kings 3:2](../03/02.md). Alternate translation: “what was evil in Yahweh’s judgment” or “what Yahweh considers to be evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: came with all his army against Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: The name “Jerusalem” is a metonym for the people who lived in it. Alternate translation: “came with his whole army to fight against the people of Jerusalem” or “came with his whole army to conquer Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Then the city was broken into
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “Then the Babylonian army broke into the city” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: All his army was scattered away from him
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “His whole army ran away from him” or “The Chaldeans chased away his whole army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they slaughtered them before his eyes
OccurrenceNote: The eyes are synecdoche for the whole person. Alternate translation: “they forced king Zedekiah to watch them kill his sons” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: he put out his eyes
OccurrenceNote: “Nebuchadnezzar put out Zedekiah’s eyes.” It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people might have helped Nebuchadnezzar do this. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: The pots for removing ashes
OccurrenceNote: You may need to make explicit which ashes are spoken of. Alternate translation: “The pots that were used for removing ashes from the altar” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: put them to death
OccurrenceNote: This is a polite way of saying “killed them.” It might be best to translate so that the reader understands that other people might have helped the king do this. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Judah went out of its land
OccurrenceNote: Judah, the name of the people group, is a metonym for the people themselves. Alternate translation: “the people of Judah went out of their land” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: all the people
OccurrenceNote: This is a generalization. Alternate translation: “many people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: from the least to the greatest
OccurrenceNote: This is a merism that means “everyone,” which is a generalization. Alternate translation: “from the least important to the most important” or “everyone” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: a seat more honorable than that of the other kings
OccurrenceNote: Giving a good place at the dining table is a metonym for honoring him. Alternate translation: “more honor than the other kings” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: removed Jehoiachin’s prison clothes
OccurrenceNote: The act of removing Jehoiachins’ prison clothes represents making him a free man. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: A regular food allowance was given to him
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The king made sure that he had a regular food allowance” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: who were born to him by Shua’s daughter, a Canaanite woman
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “his sons whom Shua’s daughter, a Canaanite woman, bore” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: in the sight of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The sight of Yahweh represents his judgment or evaluation. Alternate translation: “as Yahweh judged” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Yahweh killed him
OccurrenceNote: The reader should understand that Yahweh may have had a person kill Er. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the second … the third
OccurrenceNote: The word “son” is understood. Also, the numbers are in ordinal form. Alternate translation: “the second son … the third son” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-ordinal]])

GLQuote: the fourth … the fifth
OccurrenceNote: The word “son” is understood. Also, the numbers are in ordinal form. Alternate translation: “the fourth son … the fifth son” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-ordinal]])

GLQuote: the sixth … the seventh
OccurrenceNote: The word “son” is understood. Also, the numbers are in ordinal form. Alternate translation: “the sixth son … the seventh son” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-ordinal]])

GLQuote: Caleb went in to Ephrathah
OccurrenceNote: This is a euphemism. Alternate translation: “Caleb had sexual relations with Ephrathah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: your hand will be with me
OccurrenceNote: Possible meanings are that God’s **hand:** is: (1) a metonym for his guidance, his power, or his protection. Alternate translation: “you will guide me” or “you will make me prosper” or “you will protect me” or (2) a synecdoche for himself. Alternate translation: “you will be with me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: granted him his prayer
OccurrenceNote: The words “his prayer” are a metonym for what Jabez asked in the prayer. Alternate translation: “did what Jabez had asked him to do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: their clans increased greatly
OccurrenceNote: The clan is a metonym for the people in the clan. Alternate translation: “the number of people in their clans increased greatly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: but his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “but Israel gave Reuben’s birthright to the sons of Joseph, another of Israel’s sons” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Reuben had defiled his father’s couch
OccurrenceNote: This is a polite way to speak about Reuben sleeping with his father’s secondary wife. The couch is the place where a man and his wife would have slept together. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: So he is not recorded as being the oldest son
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “So the family history does not list Reuben as the oldest son” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: listed according to their genealogical records
OccurrenceNote: This can start a new sentence: “Their genealogical records list them as” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: lived in the Hagrites’ tents
OccurrenceNote: The tents are a synecdoche for the land and the buildings on the land. Alternate translation: “took over all the Hagrites’ land and buildings” or “lived in all the Hagrite territory” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: All these were listed by genealogical records
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “Genealogical records listed them all” or “The records of their family’s ancestry listed them all” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: who carried shield and sword, and who drew the bow
OccurrenceNote: The soldiers are described as skilled in warfare by the weapons they carried. Alternate translation: “who were all trained to fight well in battles” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: Solomon built
OccurrenceNote: The reader should understand that Solomon probably hired workers to do the work. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: exiled Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar
OccurrenceNote: The power Nebuchadnezzar has through his army is described as the part of his body (“hand”) he uses to direct his army. Alternate translation: “allowed Nebuchadnezzar’s army to defeat the armies of Judah and Jerusalem and take the people into captivity” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: according to the instructions given to them
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “according to the instructions that David gave them” or “according to the instructions they received” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: who stood at his right hand
OccurrenceNote: The authority of a person is described by where they stand. The right side of a person is the place where the person with the most authority stands. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Their associates, the Levites, were assigned to do
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “God had assigned their associates, the Levites, to do” or “It was the duty of their fellow workers, the Levites, to do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: These are the locations where Aaron’s descendants were assigned to live
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “These are the places where God assigned Aaron’s descendants to live” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Kohathites (the first lot was theirs)
OccurrenceNote: The Israelites drew lots to decide where people would live. Alternate translation: “Kohathites. The first lot that they drew was theirs” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Issachar received from the tribe of Asher
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The tribe of Asher gave Issachar” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: They received from the tribe of Naphtali
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The tribe of Naphtali gave them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: The rest … descendants received from the tribe of Zebulun
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The tribe of Zebulun gave the rest … descendants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: from the tribe of Reuben, across … Jericho, they received
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “the tribe of Reuben, across … Jericho, gave them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: The Levites received from the tribe of Gad
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The tribe of Gad gave the Levites” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Ezer and Elead were killed by men of Gath, natives in the land
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “Men of Gath, the natives in the land, killed Ezer and Elead” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: He went in to his wife
OccurrenceNote: This is a euphemism. Alternate translation: “he had sexual relations with his wife” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: Their possessions and residences were Bethel … villages
OccurrenceNote: The abstract nouns “possessions” and “residences” can be translated with verbal phrases. Alternate translation: “They possessed and resided in Bethel … villages” or “They owned and lived in Bethel … villages” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: The father of Gibeon, Jeiel, whose wife’s name was Maakah, lived in Gibeon
OccurrenceNote: Here “father of” refers to Jeiel’s status as the leading person in the city of Gibeon. Alternate translation: “Jeiel, the leader of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maakah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: all Israel was recorded in genealogies
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. The reader should understand that the people who wrote the genealogies included the names of the people who had already died. Alternate translation: “The Israelites recorded all of themselves in genealogies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: They were recorded in the book … Israel
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “They wrote the names in the book … Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they were carried away in exile
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The Babylonians carried them away in exile” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: the tent
OccurrenceNote: This is a metonym for the second temple, which the people built after they returned from Babylon. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: who were chosen as gatekeepers
OccurrenceNote: It is not clear who chose these men, so if you have to translate in active form, use your language’s most general way of doing so. Alternate translation: “whom they had chosen to be gatekeepers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Their names were recorded in the people’s records in their villages
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “The records in peoples’ villages included the names of these men” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: gatekeepers were posted
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “men guarded the entrances” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: the four leaders … were assigned to guard the rooms
OccurrenceNote: It is not clear who assigned these men, so if you have to translate in active form, use your language’s most general way of doing so. Alternate translation: “they assigned the four leaders … to guard the rooms” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they counted the articles when they were brought in and when they were taken out
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “they counted the articles that people took out to use, and they counted the articles when people brought them back” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Some of them also were assigned to take care of
OccurrenceNote: It is not clear who assigned these men, so if you have to translate in active form, use your language’s most general way of doing so. Alternate translation: “The leaders also assigned some of them to take care of” or “Some of them also took care of” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: day and night
OccurrenceNote: This means “at all times” and can be translated using a phrase or word from your language or culture that gives the same meaning. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: Every man of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell down dead on Mount Gilboa
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that these men were Israelite soldiers. Alternate translation: “The whole army of Israel ran away from the Philistines” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Every man of Israel … fell down dead
OccurrenceNote: This is probably a generalization. It seems that while all the soldiers did run away, not all of them died. Alternate translation: “Every man of Israel … most of them died” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: thrust me through with it
OccurrenceNote: The action of stabbing is a metonym for the result, death. Alternate translation: “kill me with it” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: these uncircumcised will come
OccurrenceNote: The nominal adjective “uncircumcised” can be stated as an adjective. Alternate translation: “these people who are uncircumcised will come” or “these uncircumcised people will come” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: these uncircumcised
OccurrenceNote: Here “uncircumcised” represents people who do not belong to Yahweh. Alternate translation: “these people who do not belong to Yahweh” or “these heathen Philistines” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: fell on it
OccurrenceNote: Saul probably stuck the handle into the ground and leaned on the point so the sword would go through his body as he fell down. The action is a metonym for the result, death. Alternate translation: “killed himself with it” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: fell on his sword
OccurrenceNote: He probably stuck the handle into the ground and leaned on the point so the sword would go through his body as he fell down. The action is a metonym for the result, death. See how you translated this in [1 Chronicles 10:4](../10/04.md). Alternate translation: “killed himself with his sword” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: and his three sons
OccurrenceNote: The word “died” is understood from the previous phrase. It can be repeated. Alternate translation: “and his 3 sons died” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-numbers]])

GLQuote: When every man of Israel
OccurrenceNote: This is probably a generalization. Alternate translation: “When the men of Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: Saul and his sons fallen
OccurrenceNote: Here “fallen” is a polite way to refer to someone who died in battle. Alternate translation: “Saul and his sons dead” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: to carry the news
OccurrenceNote: A person telling others about something that has happened is spoken of as if the person were carrying a solid object and giving it to those other people. Alternate translation: “to tell what had happened” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: When all Jabesh Gilead heard of all that the Philistines
OccurrenceNote: Both instances of the word “all” are generalizations. The name of the town is a metonym for the people who live in the town, and the people group name is a metonym for that people group’s soldiers. Alternate translation: “When the people of Jabesh Gilead heard what the soldiers of the Philistine army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: their bones
OccurrenceNote: The bones are a synecdoche for the dead bodies. Alternate translation: “their bodies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: turned over the kingdom to David son of Jesse
OccurrenceNote: Here “turned over the kingdom” is an idiom that means to give someone authority over a kingdom. Alternate translation: “made David, son of Jesse, king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: all Israel came to David
OccurrenceNote: This is a generalization that means people from every tribe in Israel came to David, but not every individual. Alternate translation: “people from throughout Israel came to David” or “people from every tribe in Israel came to David” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: we are your flesh and bone
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means that they are relatives. Alternate translation: “we are your relatives” or “we have the same ancestors as you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will become a ruler over my people Israel
OccurrenceNote: These two clauses mean basically the same thing and emphasize that Yahweh had chosen David to be king. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: You will shepherd my people Israel
OccurrenceNote: Here ruling over the people is spoken of as shepherding them. Alternate translation: “‘You will care for my people Israel” or “You will lead my people Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the word of Yahweh that had been declared by Samuel
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the word of Yahweh that Samuel had declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: David and all Israel
OccurrenceNote: Here the phrase “all Israel” represents the entire Israelite army. Alternate translation: “David and all the Israelite army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: David took the stronghold of Zion
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “took” is an idiom that means “captured” or “conquered.” Since David led the army, his name here is a synecdoche for the whole army who attacked the city. Alternate translation: “David captured the stronghold of Zion” or “David and the Israelite army captured the stronghold of Zion” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: so he was made the chief
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “so David made Joab the chief” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: He built the city all around … Joab restored the rest of the city
OccurrenceNote: The word “he” refers to David. The reader should understand that David and Joab were probably in charge of other men who made the fortifications. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom … to make him king
OccurrenceNote: This phrase means that both the leaders of David’s army, and the full army, helped David to establish himself as king over Israel. Alternate translation: “who strongly supported David’s kingdom … to make him king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: cut down the Philistines
OccurrenceNote: This means that they killed the Philistine soldiers with their swords. Alternate translation: “killed the Philistines” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: the well at Bethlehem, the well that is by the gate
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases refer to the same well. The second specifies which well in Bethlehem. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: the well of Bethlehem, the well at the gate
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases refer to the same well. The second specifies which well in Bethlehem. See how you translated a similar phrase in [1 Chronicles 11:17](../11/17.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: he poured it out to Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: This means that he poured out the water as an offering to Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Should I drink the blood of these men who have risked their lives?
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of the water as if it were blood because the men risked their lives to bring the water to him. He uses a question to emphasize this. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “I should not drink this water, which would be like drinking the blood of these men who have risked their lives to bring it to me.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: He is mentioned along with the Three
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People often mentioned him when they spoke of the Three” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Of the Three, he was given double honor and became
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This could mean: (1) that he received double the honor that the Three received. Alternate translation: “People gave him twice as much honor as they gave the Three and he became” or (2) the Three honored him more than they honored others. Alternate translation: “The Three honored him more than they honored others and he became” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: a spear like a weaver’s beam
OccurrenceNote: This compares the size of the spear with the size of a weaver’s beam. Alternate translation: “a spear the size of a weaver’s beam” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: he went down to him
OccurrenceNote: “Benaiah went down to the Egyptian.” This idiom means that he met him in battle. Alternate translation: “he attacked him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: he was named alongside the three mighty men
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “people praised him like they praised the three mighty men” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: He was more highly regarded than the thirty soldiers in general, but he was not regarded quite as highly as the three mighty men
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “The people respected him more than the 30 soldiers, but not as much as the 3 most elite soldiers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: while he was still banished from the presence of
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “during the time when he could not be in the presence of” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: whose faces were as fierce as the faces of lions
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “faces” represents the men and the lions. Their faces express the fierceness with which they fight battles. Alternate translation: “who were as fierce in battle as lions hunting prey” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: They were as swift as gazelles on the mountains
OccurrenceNote: This hyperbole compares how swiftly these men were able to run with how swiftly gazelles are able to run over rugged mountain terrain. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: may the God of our ancestors see
OccurrenceNote: What God will see may be supplied in translation. Alternate translation: “may the God of our ancestors see what you intend to do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the Spirit came on Amasai
OccurrenceNote: The Spirit empowering Amasai is spoken of as if the Spirit came on him. Alternate translation: “the Spirit empowered Amasai” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: We are yours, David. We are on your side, son of Jesse
OccurrenceNote: These phrases share similar meanings. The idioms “we are yours” and “we are on your side” both mean that the men support David. Alternate translation: “We are devoted to you, David. We support you, son of Jesse” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Peace, may peace be to whoever helps you
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “peace” refers to prosperity and well-being. The word is repeated to emphasize great prosperity. Alternate translation: “May whoever helps you greatly prosper” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: a great army, like the army of God
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) the phrase “like the army of God” means “like an army that God assembled” or (2) the word “God” is used as an idiom that refers to the great size of the army. Alternate translation: “a very large army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him
OccurrenceNote: The men making David king in place of Saul is spoken of as if they gave possession of Saul’s kingdom to David. Alternate translation: “to make David king in place of Saul” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: ready to give undivided loyalty
OccurrenceNote: It is implicit that they would give loyalty to David. Alternate translation: “ready to give undivided loyalty to David” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Israel was celebrating
OccurrenceNote: The word “Israel” represents the people who make up the nation. Alternate translation: “the people of Israel were celebrating” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: all the assembly of Israel
OccurrenceNote: This refers to all of the Israelites who were assembled in this place. Alternate translation: “all of the Israelites who were assembled there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: if this comes from Yahweh our God
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means that this action is something that Yahweh approves. Alternate translation: “if this is something that Yahweh our God approves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Let them be told to join us
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Let messengers tell them to join us” or “Let them join us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they seemed right in the eyes of all the people
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “eyes” represents seeing, and seeing represents thoughts or judgment. Alternate translation: “all the people considered these things to be right” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: David assembled all Israel together
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “all” is a generalization. The phrase means that David assembled people from all over Israel, not that he assembled every person in Israel. Alternate translation: “David assembled people together from all Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: to bring up from there the ark of God
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they are taking the ark to Jerusalem. Alternate translation: “to take to Jerusalem the ark of God” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: which is called by Yahweh’s name
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This could mean: (1) the idiom “called by … name” refers to a person owning the thing. Alternate translation: “which belongs to Yahweh” or (2) the ark has Yahweh’s name written on it. Alternate translation: “which bears Yahweh’s name” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: who sits enthroned over the cherubim
OccurrenceNote: You may need to make explicit that the cherubim are those on the lid of the ark of the covenant. The biblical writers often spoke of the ark of the covenant as if it were Yahweh’s footstool upon which he rested his feet as he sat on his throne in heaven above. Alternate translation: “who sits on his throne above the cherubim on the ark of the covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: David and all Israel
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “all” is a generalization. Alternate translation: “David and all of the Israelites who were present” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: the anger of Yahweh burned against Uzzah
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s anger is spoken of as if it were a fire that burned the one with whom Yahweh is angry. Alternate translation: “Yahweh was very angry with Uzzah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: That place is called
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People call that place” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: How can I bring the ark of God home to me?
OccurrenceNote: David uses this question to emphasize that he is afraid to take the ark to Jerusalem. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “I am too afraid to bring the ark of Yahweh with me to Jerusalem.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Yahweh blessed his house
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “house” is a metonym for his family. Alternate translation: “Yahweh blessed his family” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: his kingdom was exalted on high
OccurrenceNote: The idiom “exalted on high” means that Yahweh had given great honor to David’s kingdom. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh had exalted David’s kingdom on high” or “Yahweh had given great honor to David’s kingdom” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: David had been anointed as king
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the elders of Israel had anointed David as king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: went out against them
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that David led his army out to fight against them. Alternate translation: “led his army out to fight against them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: give them to you
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means that Yahweh will enable David to have victory over them. Alternate translation: “give you victory over them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: God has burst through my enemies … like a bursting flood of water
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of God easily defeating David’s enemies as if God had burst through them, like a flood bursts through anything in its path. Alternate translation: “God has easily defeated my enemies … like a flood easily bursts through everything” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: by my hand
OccurrenceNote: This refers to David’s resources. Alternate translation: “using my army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: that they should be burned
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “to burn their false gods” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: When you hear the sound of marching in the wind blowing through the balsam treetops
OccurrenceNote: This speaks of the sound of the leaves rustling as wind blows through them as if it were the sound of marching. Alternate translation: “When the wind blowing through the tops of the balsam trees sounds like men marching” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: David’s fame went out into all lands
OccurrenceNote: People in every land hearing of David’s reputation is spoken of as if David’s fame traveled to those lands. Alternate translation: “People far away heard about David’s fame” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: David built houses for himself … He prepared
OccurrenceNote: It might be best to translate this so that the reader understands that David had other people do this for him. Alternate translation: “David had workers build houses for him … He had them prepare” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: they had been chosen by Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh had chosen them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “all” is a generalization. The phrase “all Israel” means that David assembled people from all over Israel, not that he assembled every person in Israel. Alternate translation: “David assembled at Jerusalem people from all over Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: broke out against us
OccurrenceNote: The idiom to “break out against” means to act violently toward someone. Alternate translation: “acted violently toward us” or “attacked us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: we did not seek him
OccurrenceNote: Here seeking Yahweh means to seek his counsel. Alternate translation: “we did not ask him for instructions” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the rules given by the word of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The word “word” can be translated with a verb. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the rules that the word of Yahweh had given” or “the rules that Yahweh had spoken” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: lifting up their voices
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means to sing loudly. Alternate translation: “singing loudly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Mikneiah, Obed Edom, and Jeiel, the gatekeepers
OccurrenceNote: The word “gatekeepers” refers to people who guard gates or entryways. Here it refers to guarding access to the ark of the covenant and applies to Obed Edom and Jeiel. Alternate translation: “Mikneiah, and the gatekeepers, Obed Edom and Jeiel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: The musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “The Levites appointed the musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Kenaniah, the leader of the song with the singers
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “David, the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Kenaniah, the leader of the song with the singers all wore fine linen robes” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: So all Israel brought up the ark
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “all” is a generalization. Alternate translation: “So a great crowd of Israelites brought up the ark” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: she despised him in her heart
OccurrenceNote: Here “heart” represents thoughts or emotions. Alternate translation: “she despised him” or “she hated him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings
OccurrenceNote: This is a metonym for David directing the priests, who performed the actual sacrifices. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: To bless “in the name of Yahweh” means to bless with Yahweh’s power and authority or as his representative. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He distributed to every Israelite
OccurrenceNote: This was done under David’s authority and direction. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: call on his name
OccurrenceNote: Here “his name” represents Yahweh. Alternate translation: “call on Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the nations
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the people in the nations. Alternate translation: “the people of the nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Boast in his holy name
OccurrenceNote: Here “his holy name” represents Yahweh. Alternate translation: “Boast in who Yahweh is” or “Boast in Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice
OccurrenceNote: - Here “the heart” represents the person who seeks Yahweh. Alternate translation: “let the people who seek Yahweh rejoice” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Seek Yahweh and his strength
OccurrenceNote: To “seek Yahweh’s strength” means to ask him to strengthen you. Alternate translation: “Seek Yahweh and ask him to give you his strength” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: his miracles and
OccurrenceNote: The understood verb may be supplied. Alternate translation: “remember his miracles and” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: decrees from his mouth
OccurrenceNote: Here “mouth” refers to the things that Yahweh spoke. Alternate translation: “decrees that he has spoken” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: you descendants of Israel his servant, you people of Jacob, his chosen ones
OccurrenceNote: These phrases share similar meanings and are used for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: His decrees are on all the earth
OccurrenceNote: Here “all the earth” refers to all the people of the earth. Alternate translation: “His laws are for all the people of the earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Keep his covenant … for a thousand generations
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases share similar meanings and are used together for emphasis. Here “word” refers to the covenant. Alternate translation: “Keep his covenant in mind forever, the promise that he made for a thousand generations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Keep his covenant in mind
OccurrenceNote: This means to remember and think about his covenant. Alternate translation: “Remember his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: He calls to mind
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “calls to mind” means to remember something. Alternate translation: “He remembers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the covenant that he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac
OccurrenceNote: Both “the covenant” and “the oath” refer to the same promise that Yahweh made to his people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his oath to Isaac
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the oath that he had previously made to Issac. Alternate translation: “his oath that he made to Isaac” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: strangers in the land
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that “the land” refers to Canaan. Alternate translation: “foreigners in the land of Canaan” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings and are used together for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Do not touch my anointed ones
OccurrenceNote: Here “touch” means to harm. It is an exaggeration Yahweh used to strengthen his warning to not harm his people. Alternate translation: “Do not harm the people I have anointed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: all the earth
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the people of the earth. Alternate translation: “all you people who live on the earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: announce his salvation
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **salvation**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “save.” Alternate translation: “announce that he has saved us” or “tell people that he is the one who saves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Yahweh is great and is to be praised greatly
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “Yahweh is great. Praise him greatly” or “Yahweh is great, and people should praise him greatly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: he is to be feared above all other gods
OccurrenceNote: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: “fear him above all other gods” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Splendor and majesty are in his presence
OccurrenceNote: The author speaks as if splendor and majesty are people who can stand before a king. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Strength and joy are in his place
OccurrenceNote: The author speaks as if strength and joy are people who can be in Yahweh’s sanctuary. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength
OccurrenceNote: The abstract nouns “glory” and “strength” can be stated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “praise Yahweh because he is glorious and strong” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Ascribe to Yahweh the glory his name deserves
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **glory**, you could express the same idea with a verb or adjective. Alternate translation: “Glorify Yahweh just as his name deserves” or “Proclaim that Yahweh is glorious just as his name deserves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: his name deserves
OccurrenceNote: Here “his name” refers to the person of God. Alternate translation: “due to him” or “he deserves” or “he is worthy to receive” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Bow down to Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The implied information is that the people were to bow down in worship. Alternate translation: “Bow down to worship Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-symaction]])

GLQuote: in the splendor of holiness
OccurrenceNote: The abstract nouns “splendor” and “holiness” can be translated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “because he is gloriously beautiful and holy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: all the earth
OccurrenceNote: This is a metonym for all the people who live on the earth. Alternate translation: “all the people of the earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) the heavens and the earth are spoken of as if they have emotions like people. Alternate translation: “Let it be as if the heavens are glad and the earth rejoices” or (2) “the heavens” and “the earth” are metonyms for those who dwell in those places. Alternate translation: “Let those who live in the heavens be glad and let those who live on the earth rejoice” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: that which fills it shout with joy
OccurrenceNote: The implied information is that this refers to all the creatures living in the sea. They are spoken of as if they should shout with joy like people might do. Alternate translation: “the sea creatures shout joyfully” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Let the fields be joyful, and all that is in them
OccurrenceNote: “Let the fields and all that is in them be joyful.” The author speaks as if the fields and the animals that live in them have emotions like people. Alternate translation: “Let it be as if the fields themselves and all the animals that live in them are rejoicing” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: let the trees in the forest shout for joy
OccurrenceNote: This speaks about the trees as if they were people who could shout for joy. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: for his covenant faithfulness endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “faithfully” or “faithful.” Alternate translation: “for he faithfully loves us forever” or “for he is faithful to his covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: from the other nations
OccurrenceNote: Here “the other nations” represents the people in those nations. Alternate translation: “from the people of other nations” or “from the armies of other nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: give thanks to your holy name
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh is referred to by his “holy name.” Alternate translation: “give thanks to you” or “give thanks to Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: from everlasting to everlasting
OccurrenceNote: This refers to two extremes and means for all time. Alternate translation: “for all eternity” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: All the people
OccurrenceNote: This is a generalization that refers to the group of people assembled to worship Yahweh. Alternate translation: “The people” or “Everyone who was there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: as every day’s work required
OccurrenceNote: The implied information is that they were to perform the daily duties that were given in the law of Yahweh. Alternate translation: “as was required every day by the law” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: guarded the gate
OccurrenceNote: The implied information is that they were to guard the entrance to the tabernacle. Alternate translation: “guarded the tabernacle gate” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: I am living in a house of cedar
OccurrenceNote: Cedar is a kind of tree that is known for its strength. If you have an equivalent type of tree in your culture, you can use that name, otherwise you can reword this. Alternate translation: “I am living in a strong, permanent house” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the ark of the covenant of Yahweh is staying under a tent
OccurrenceNote: Tents are temporary dwellings. If you do not have tents in your culture, you can word this differently. Alternate translation: “the ark of the covenant of Yahweh is staying in a temporary place” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: do what is in your heart
OccurrenceNote: Here “heart” represents the mind. Alternate translation: “do what you think you should” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: God is with you
OccurrenceNote: Here “with you” means God is helping and blessing David. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the word of God came to Nathan, saying,
OccurrenceNote: The idiom “the word of God came to” is used to introduce a special message from God. Alternate translation: “God gave a message to Nathan. He said,” or “God spoke this message to Nathan:” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Go and tell David my servant, ‘This is what Yahweh says: You will not build me a house in which to live
OccurrenceNote: This has quotations within quotations. It may be necessary to translate them as indirect quotations. Alternate translation: “Go and tell David my servant that he will not be the one to build a house in which I will live” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-quotesinquotes]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-quotations]])

GLQuote: that I brought up Israel
OccurrenceNote: The implied information is that this refers to God bringing up Israel out of the land of Egypt. Alternate translation: “that I brought the Israelites to the promised land from the land of Egypt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: a tent, a tabernacle
OccurrenceNote: Both the words “tent” and “tabernacle” describe the same thing and emphasize that he had lived in a place that was not a permanent building. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: did I ever say anything to any of Israel’s leaders whom I appointed to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”
OccurrenceNote: This has a quotation within a quotation. The direct quotation can be stated as an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: “did I ever ask any of Israel’s leaders, whom I appointed to shepherd my people, why they had not built me a house of cedar?” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-quotesinquotes]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-quotations]])

GLQuote: did I ever say anything to any of Israel’s leaders
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses a question to emphasize that he never asked any of Israel’s leaders to build him a house. Alternate translation: “I never said anything to any of Israel’s leaders” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: whom I appointed to shepherd my people
OccurrenceNote: Those who are leaders of the people of Israel are spoken of as if they were shepherds and the people were sheep. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Why have you not built me a house of cedar?
OccurrenceNote: If Yahweh had asked the leaders this question, he would have been using a question to scold them for not building him a house of cedar. But, Yahweh said previously that he did not ask them this question. Alternate translation: “You should have built me a house of cedar.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: I took you from the pasture
OccurrenceNote: David’s job as a shepherd is referred to by the place he watched his sheep. Alternate translation: “I took you from your job as a shepherd” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: I have been with you
OccurrenceNote: Here “with you” means that Yahweh has helped and blessed David. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: cut off all your enemies
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh destroying David’s enemies is spoken of as if Yahweh cut them off, as one would cut a piece of cloth or cut a branch from a tree. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will make you a name
OccurrenceNote: Here “name” represents a person’s reputation. Alternate translation: “I will make your name to be great and well known” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: will plant them there
OccurrenceNote: God causing the people to live in the land permanently and securely is spoken of as if he would plant them in the land. Alternate translation: “I will settle them there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: be troubled no more
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “no one will ever trouble them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: from the days
OccurrenceNote: Here “days” represents a longer period of time. Alternate translation: “from the time” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: to be over my people Israel
OccurrenceNote: To be in authority is referred to as being over someone. Alternate translation: “to rule my people Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: build you a house
OccurrenceNote: Here the metonym “house” refers to David’s ancestors continuing on as the rulers of Israel. In [1 Chronicles 17:4](../17/04.md) God told David he would not be the one to build a house for Yahweh. There “house” represented a temple. If your language has a word that can express both ideas, use it here and in 17:4. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: when your days are fulfilled for you to go to your fathers
OccurrenceNote: The two phrases “when your days are fulfilled” and “go to your fathers” have similar meanings and are combined for emphasis. They both are polite ways to refer to death and dying. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: I will raise up your descendant after you
OccurrenceNote: God appointing David’s descendant is spoken of as if Yahweh would raise or lift him up. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will establish his throne forever
OccurrenceNote: The right to rule as king is described by the place where a king sits. Alternate translation: “I will make his rule over Israel to last forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: I will not take my covenant faithfulness away from him, as I took it from Saul
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “faithfully.” Alternate translation: “I will never stop faithfully loving him, as I stopped loving Saul” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: I will set him over my house and in my kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings and emphasize that David’s dynasty will last forever. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his throne will be established forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “I will establish his throne forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: his throne
OccurrenceNote: A king’s right to rule is referred to by the place a king sits. Alternate translation: “his right to rule” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: all these words
OccurrenceNote: Here “words” represents what Yahweh said. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Who am I, Yahweh God, and what is my family, that you have brought me to this point?
OccurrenceNote: - David asks this question to express the deep emotion he felt from hearing Yahweh’s proclamation. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement.
