OccurrenceNote: David did not purposefully mix his drink with tears; rather his tear would have fallen into his cup while he mourned and wept. Alternate translation: “my tears fall into the cup that I drink” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: you have lifted me up to throw me down
OccurrenceNote: God has not literally lifted and thrown David’s body to the ground; rather David says this to describe what he is feeling and experiencing. Alternate translation: “it is like you have lifted me up to throw me down” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: My days are like a shadow that fades
OccurrenceNote: David compares his time left to live on earth to a fading shadow. Alternate translation: “My time to remain alive is short like an evening shadow that will soon be gone” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: I have withered like grass
OccurrenceNote: As David’s body becomes weak and he is nearing the end of his life, he compares himself to withering grass. Alternate translation: “my body has become weak like withered grass” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: have mercy on Zion
OccurrenceNote: Here “Zion” refers to the people who live in Zion. Alternate translation: “have mercy on the people of Zion” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: hold her stones dear
OccurrenceNote: The “stones” refer to the stones that were part of the city walls before they were destroyed. Alternate translation: “still love the stones that were formerly in the city walls” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: your name
OccurrenceNote: Here “your name” refers to Yahweh. Alternate translation: “you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: will honor your glory
OccurrenceNote: The people will honor Yahweh because of his glory. Here Yahweh is referred to by his glory. Alternate translation: “will honor you because you are glorious” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: the destitute
OccurrenceNote: This refers to destitute people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: he will not reject their prayer
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated in positive form. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will accept their prayers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublenegatives]])

GLQuote: This will be written for future generations
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “I will write this for future generations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: For he has looked down from the holy heights; from heaven Yahweh has viewed
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meaning and are used together for emphasize how God looks down from heaven. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: those who were condemned to death
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “those whom the authorities had sentenced to die” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: proclaim the name of Yahweh in Zion and his praise in Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have the same meaning and emphasize the idea of praising the name of Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: taken away my strength
OccurrenceNote: David describes God causing him to become weak as if his strength were a physical item that could be taken away from him. Alternate translation: “has caused me to become weak” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my days
OccurrenceNote: The word “days” here refers to his life. Alternate translation: “my life” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: do not take me away
OccurrenceNote: David is asking God to not let him die. Alternate translation: “do not take me away from the earth” or “do not let me die” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: your years will have no end
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes the length of time that God is alive as his “years.” This can be written in positive form. Alternate translation: “you will live forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublenegatives]])

GLQuote: live in your presence
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes the descendants being protected by Yahweh as being in his presence. Alternate translation: “be protected as they live in your presence” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I give praise to Yahweh with all my life, and with all that is within me, I give praise to his holy name
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean basically the same thing and emphasize how much he will praise Yahweh. Alternate translation: “I will praise Yahweh with all that I am” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: give praise to his holy name
OccurrenceNote: This refers to praising Yahweh’s name as Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: all that is within me
OccurrenceNote: “all of me” or “all that I am.” David uses this phrase to refer to himself and to emphasize his devotion to Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: He redeems your life from destruction
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh keeps him alive. Alternate translation: “He saves me from dying” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he crowns you with covenant faithfulness and acts of tender mercy
OccurrenceNote: Here blessing someone and treating them with great honor is described as if it were placing a crown on that person’s head. The abstract nouns “faithfulness” and “mercy” can be translated with adverbs. Alternate translation: “he blesses you by acting faithfully and mercifully towards you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: He satisfies your life with good things
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “your life” refers to “you,” but it emphasizes that Yahweh gives blessings throughout life. Alternate translation: “He satisfies you with good things through your life” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: your youth is renewed like the eagle
OccurrenceNote: Having your “youth renewed” means to feel young again. Here David compares this feeling of youth to the swiftness and strength of an eagle. Alternate translation: “you feel young and are strong like an eagle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: your youth
OccurrenceNote: The word “youth” refers to the strength one had as a young adult. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: all who are oppressed
OccurrenceNote: Who is doing the oppressing can be stated explicitly. Alternate translation: “all who are oppressed by men” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: his deeds to the descendants of Israel
OccurrenceNote: The words “he made known” are understood from the previous phrase. They may be repeated here. Alternate translation: “he made known his deeds to the descendants of Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: He will not always discipline; he is not always angry
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings. The second one strengthens the thought in the first. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: He does not deal with us … or repay us
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases are parallel and emphasize that God does not punish us as we deserve. Alternate translation: “He does not repay us with the punishment we deserve for our sins” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: For as the skies are high … toward those who honor him
OccurrenceNote: The simile compares the great distance between heaven and earth to the greatness of God’s love for his people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: so great is his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “so he is very faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: As far as the east … removed the guilt of our sins from us
OccurrenceNote: The distance between east and west is so far that it cannot be measured. In this simile, that distance is being compared to how far God moves our guilt away from us. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: As a father has compassion … on those who honor him
OccurrenceNote: Here the author compares a father’s compassion for his children to Yahweh’s compassion for those who honor him. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: how we are formed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “what our bodies are like” or “how he formed our bodies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: he knows that we are dust
OccurrenceNote: When Yahweh created Adam the first man he created him from dust. Alternate translation: “he remembers that he created us from dust” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: As for man, his days are like grass
OccurrenceNote: In this simile, the length of man’s life is being compared to the short length of time that grass grows before it dies. Alternate translation: “The length of man’s life is short like that of grass” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: he flourishes like a flower in a field
OccurrenceNote: In this simile, how man grows over time is compared to how a flower grows. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: The wind blows over it, and it disappears … where it once grew
OccurrenceNote: These phrases continue to talk about flowers and grass. They compare how flowers and grass die to how man dies. Alternate translation: “The wind blows over the flowers and grass and they disappear, and no one can tell where they once grew—it is the same way with man” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: the covenant faithfulness of Yahweh is
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Yahweh is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: is from everlasting to everlasting
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh’s love continues forever. Alternate translation: “will continue forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: They keep his covenant and remember to obey his instructions
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Yahweh has established his throne in the heavens
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh’s reign as king is referred to as his “throne.” Alternate translation: “Yahweh has taken his seat in the heavens where he rules as king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: his kingdom rules
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh is referred to by “his kingdom” to emphasize his authority as king. Alternate translation: “he rules” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: carry out his will
OccurrenceNote: This is an idiom meaning to “do his will.” Alternate translation: “do his will” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: with all my life
OccurrenceNote: This phrase means that he will praise Yahweh wholeheartedly and is used to emphasize his devotion to him. Alternate translation: “with all of me” or “with all my soul” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: with all my life
OccurrenceNote: This phrase means that he will praise Yahweh wholeheartedly and is used to emphasize his devotion to him. Alternate translation: “with all of me” or “with all my soul”(See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: you are clothed with splendor and majesty
OccurrenceNote: The words “splendor” and “majesty” have similar meanings and emphasize the greatness of Yahweh’s glory. They are described as clothing Yahweh like a garment. Alternate translation: “you have splendor and majesty all around you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: You cover yourself with light as with a garment
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh is described as being covered with light as if the light were a garment around him. Alternate translation: “You are covered in light” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: you spread out the heavens like a tent curtain
OccurrenceNote: Here God is described as spreading out the heavens like someone spreads out a tent when setting it up. Alternate translation: “you spread out the heavens like someone sets up a tent” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: you make the clouds your chariot
OccurrenceNote: Here the clouds are described as carrying Yahweh as if they were a chariot. Alternate translation: “you make the clouds carry you like a chariot” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you walk on the wings of the wind
OccurrenceNote: Here the blowing of the wind is described as wings on which Yahweh walks. Alternate translation: “you walk upon the wind” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: He makes the winds his messengers
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) he causes the wind to be able to carry a message like a messenger, “He makes the winds to be like his messengers” or (2) “He makes his messengers swift like the wind” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: flames of fire his servants
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “he causes flames of fire to be like his servants.” He causes fire to serve him like a servant would or (2) “he makes his servants to be like flames of fire”and (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: flames of fire his servants
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated with the implied information from the previous line. Alternate translation: “He makes the flames of fire his servants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: He laid the foundations of the earth
OccurrenceNote: Here the phrase “laid the foundations” means “created.” Alternate translation: “He created the whole earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: You covered the earth with water like a garment
OccurrenceNote: Here the water that covered the earth is being compared to how a large garment is able to completely cover something. Alternate translation: “You completely covered the earth with water” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: Your rebuke made the waters … they fled
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning and are used together to emphasize how God spoke and the waters went away. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: they fled
OccurrenceNote: Here the psalmist speaks about the waters receding as if they fled like an animal after hearing Yahweh’s voice. The word “fled” means to run away quickly. Alternate translation: “rushed away” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: The mountains rose, and the valleys spread out
OccurrenceNote: Here the psalmist speaks of God causing the mountains and valleys to move and change as if they chose to move themselves. They are described this way to emphasize God’s power. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: a boundary for them that they will not cross
OccurrenceNote: Here the psalmist speaks of God causing the waters not to cross the boundary that he created for them as if the waters themselves chose not to cross it. They are described this way to emphasize God’s authority over them. Alternate translation: “a boundary for them that they cannot cross” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: the wild donkeys quench their thirst
OccurrenceNote: It can be stated clearly that they quench their thirst by drinking the water. Alternate translation: “the wild donkeys drink the water to quench their thirst” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: they sing among the branches
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes birds chirping as if they were singing. Alternate translation: “they chirp among the tree branches” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: He waters the mountains from his water chambers in the sky
OccurrenceNote: This means that God causes it to rain. The waters are described as residing in chambers in the sky. Alternate translation: “He waters the mountains by causing the rains to fall from the sky” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: and plants for man to cultivate
OccurrenceNote: The words “he makes” and “grow” are understood from the previous phrase, and can be repeated here. Alternate translation: “and he makes the plants grow for man to cultivate” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: The trees of Yahweh get plenty of rain
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh provides plenty of rain for his trees” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: There the birds make their nests
OccurrenceNote: They makes their nests in the cedars. This can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “The birds make their nests in the cedars” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the sun knows its time
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes the sun as if it knows what time of day it is. Alternate translation: “he made the sun to set when it is time” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: overflows with your works
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes the amount of things that Yahweh had created as if they were a liquid overflowing out of a container. Alternate translation: “is filled with your work” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: deep and wide
OccurrenceNote: “it is very deep and very wide.” The depth and width of the sea emphasizes how large it is. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: both small and great
OccurrenceNote: This means creatures of all sizes. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: When you give to them, they gather
OccurrenceNote: It may be helpful to state that it is food that is given. Alternate translation: “When you give food to them, they gather it” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: when you open your hand
OccurrenceNote: This describes Yahweh as opening his hand to give food to the creatures. Alternate translation: “when you open your hand to feed them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: hide your face
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh does not look at them or pay attention to them. Alternate translation: “when you do not look upon them” or “when you ignore them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: return to dust
OccurrenceNote: This means that their bodies decay and are and become soil again. Alternate translation: “their bodies decay and return to the ground” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: When you send out your Spirit
OccurrenceNote: This refers to his Spirit being sent to give life to creatures. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: they are created
OccurrenceNote: It is Yahweh’s spirit that created them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: my thoughts be sweet
OccurrenceNote: He is comparing his thoughts to something that tastes sweet. Alternate translation: “my thoughts be pleasing” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: let the wicked be no more
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “the wicked” refers to wicked people. Alternate translation: “may wicked people disappear” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: call on his name
OccurrenceNote: Here “name” represents Yahweh. Alternate translation: “call on him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the nations
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the people in the nations. Alternate translation: “the people of the nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Boast in his holy name
OccurrenceNote: Here “name” represents Yahweh. Alternate translation: “Boast in Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice
OccurrenceNote: Here “the heart” represents the person who seeks Yahweh. Alternate translation: “let the people who seek Yahweh rejoice” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Seek Yahweh and his strength
OccurrenceNote: To “seek Yahweh’s strength” means to ask him to strengthen you. Alternate translation: “Seek Yahweh and ask him to give you his strength” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: his miracles and
OccurrenceNote: The word “recall” is understood from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: “recall his miracles and” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: the decrees from his mouth
OccurrenceNote: Here “mouth” refers to the things that he spoke. Alternate translation: “the decrees that he has spoken” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He keeps in mind … the word that he commanded
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases share similar meanings and are used together for emphasis. The word “word” refers to the covenant. Alternate translation: “He keeps in mind his covenant forever, the promise he made” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: keeps in mind
OccurrenceNote: This means to remember and think about something. Alternate translation: “remembers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: He calls to mind
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “call to mind” means to remember something. Alternate translation: “he remembers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the covenant that he made with Abraham … his oath to Isaac
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases “the covenant” and “the oath” refer to the same promise that Yahweh made to his people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his oath to Isaac
OccurrenceNote: The words “that he made” are undestood from the previous phrase. They can be repeated. Alternate translation: “his oath that he made to Isaac” or “his oath that he gave to Isaac” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: were strangers in the land
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that “the land” refers to Canaan. Alternate translation: “were foreigners in the land of Canaan” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: from nation to nation and from one kingdom to another
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings and are used together for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Do not touch my anointed ones
OccurrenceNote: Here “touch” means to harm, it’s an exaggeration Yahweh used to strengthen his warning to not harm his people. Alternate translation: “Do not harm the people I have anointed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: He called for
OccurrenceNote: “He sent.” This means that caused a famine to happen in the land. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the whole supply of bread
OccurrenceNote: Here “bread” refers to food in general. Alternate translation: “the whole supply of food” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: He sent a man ahead of them; Joseph
OccurrenceNote: It may be helpful to state that he sent him ahead of them to Egypt. Alternate translation: “He sent a man ahead of them to Egypt; he sent Joseph who” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Joseph was sold as a servant
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Joseph’s brothers sold him as a slave” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: His feet were bound by shackles; on his neck was put an iron collar
OccurrenceNote: These statements can be restated as active. Alternate translation: “The Egyptians bound his feet in shackles; they put an iron collar around his neck. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: The king sent servants to release him; the ruler of the people set him free
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning and are used together to emphasize that the king set Joseph free. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Then Israel came into Egypt
OccurrenceNote: Here “Israel” refers to Jacob. Jacob also brought his family with him. Alternate translation: “Then Israel and his family came into Egypt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Yahweh made his people fruitful
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of the increase of Israel as if they were a plant that produced a lot of fruit. “God increased the number of his people greatly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: They performed his signs among the Egyptians … his wonders in the land of Ham
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning. Alternate translation: “Moses and Aaron performed God’s miracles in Egypt among the descendants of Ham” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his wonders in the land of Ham
OccurrenceNote: The words “they performed” are understood fromt the previous phrase. They may be repeated here. Alternate translation: “and they performed his wonders in the land of Ham” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: the land of Ham
OccurrenceNote: Ham was an ancestor of the people of Egypt. Alternate translation: “the land of Ham’s descendants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He destroyed … he broke
OccurrenceNote: God caused the hail, rain, and lightning to ruin the vines and trees. Alternate translation: “He caused it to destroy … and to break” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: The locusts ate up all of the vegetation … They ate up all the crops of the ground
OccurrenceNote: These two phrase have basically the same meaning and are used together for emphasis. Alternate translation: “The insects ate all the plants and all the crops in the land” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: He killed every firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their strength
OccurrenceNote: Here the second phrase about the “firstfruits” is used to describe the “firstborn” in the first phrase. Alternate translation: “He killed every firstborn in their land, which were the firstfruits of all their strength” or “Then Yahweh killed the oldest son in every house of the people of Egypt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: He brought the Israelites out with silver and gold
OccurrenceNote: When the Israelites left Egypt they took silver and gold with them. Alternate translation: “He brought the Isrealites out of Egypt with silver and gold in their possession” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: none of his tribes stumbled on the way
OccurrenceNote: No one was left behind. This can be stated positively Alternate translation: “all of his tribes was able to make the journey” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublenegatives]])

GLQuote: Egypt was glad
OccurrenceNote: Here “Egypt” refers to the people who live in Egypt. Alternate translation: The people of Egypt were glad (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He spread a cloud for a covering
OccurrenceNote: Here the psalmist describes Yahweh placing a cloud in the sky as if he were spreading out a garment. The cloud was a “covering” to protect them from the sun. Alternate translation: “He placed a cloud in the sky to protect them from the sun and heat” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: made a fire to light up the night
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh placed a pillar of fire in the sky to give light during the night. Alternate translation: “placed a fire it the sky to light up the night” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: he brought quail
OccurrenceNote: It may be helpful to make clear that quail are small birds Yahweh sent for them to eat. Alternate translation: “Yahweh sent small birds to eat” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: with bread from heaven
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh caused manna, a type of bread, to fall from the sky. Alternate translation: “with bread that fell from the sky” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: called to mind
OccurrenceNote: This means to remember. Alternate translation: “remembered” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: He led his people out … his chosen with shouts of triumph
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning and are used together to emphasize that God’s people were joyful when he led them out of Egypt. The people were shouting joyfully. Alternate translation: “He led his chosen people out with shouts of joy and triumph” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his chosen
OccurrenceNote: Here “chosen” refers to Yahweh’s chosen people. Alternate translation: “his chosen people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: keep his statutes and obey his laws
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning and are used together for emphasis. “To keep” his statutes means to obey them. Alternate translation: “obey his laws and statutes” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: for his covenant faithfulness endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “for he remains faithful to his covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Who can recount the mighty acts of Yahweh … deeds?
OccurrenceNote: The author asks this question to praise God and does not expect an answer. Alternate translation: “No one can recount the mighty acts of Yahweh … deeds.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Call me to mind
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “call to mind” means to remember something. Alternate translation: “remember me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: of your chosen
OccurrenceNote: The word “chosen” refers to Yahweh’s chosen people. Alternate translation: “of your chosen people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: rejoice in the gladness … and glory
OccurrenceNote: These are things that David says he will do, along with “seeing the prosperity of your chosen.” The words “I will” may be repeated here. Alternate translation: “I will rejoice in the gladness … and I will glory” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: glory with your inheritance
OccurrenceNote: Here the phrase “your inheritance” refers to the Isrealites, who are Yahweh’s chosen people. Here “glory” means “to boast about” something; in this case they are boasting about Yahweh. Alternate translation: “boast of your greatness with your people” or “boast with your people about you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: they ignored your many acts of covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “they ignored the many things that you did because you are faithful to your covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: for his name’s sake
OccurrenceNote: Here “his name” refers to Yahweh. Alternate translation: “for the sake of his own reputation” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: through the depths, as through a wilderness
OccurrenceNote: Here David compares the way that Yahweh led the Isrealites through the Sea of Reeds to the way people can be led across the dry ground of a wilderness. “The depths” refers the riverbed that appeared after Yahweh parted the waters. Alternate translation: “through the Seas of Reeds on dry ground” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: He saved them from the hand … and he rescued them from the hand
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean basically the same thing and are used together to emphasize that Yahweh saved them from their enemies. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the hand of those who hated them
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to power or control. Alternate translation: “the power of those who hated them” or “the control of those who hated them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: covered their adversaries
OccurrenceNote: This is a polite way to talk about them drowning. Alternate translation: “drowned their enemies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: they did not wait for his instructions
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they did things without waiting to find out what Yahweh wanted them to go. Alternate translation: “they did things without first waiting for Yahweh’s instructions” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: but he sent a horrible disease
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks about Yahweh causing the people to be afflicted by a disease as if Yahweh sent a disease to them in the same way that someone sends a person or a messenger. Alternate translation: “but he caused them to suffer from a horrible disease” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: In the camp
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the Israelites’ camp in the wilderness. Alternate translation: “In the camp in the wilderness” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: The earth opened and swallowed up
OccurrenceNote: Here how the ground opens up and buries the people is being compared to how a creature swallows something. Alternate translation: “The earth opened and buried” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: covered the followers of Abiram
OccurrenceNote: The followers of Abiram were also buried when the earth opened and buried Dathan. Alternate translation: “it also covered the followers of Abiram” or “it also buried the followers of Abiram” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: Fire broke out among them; the fire consumed the wicked
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean the same things and are written together to emphasize how the wicked people were killed by the fire. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: They made a calf at Horeb and worshiped a cast metal figure
OccurrenceNote: This information can be reordered so that it is clear that the calf was the cast metal figure. Alternate translation: “At Horeb, they made a cast metal figure of a calf and worshiped it” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: They traded the glory of God for the image of a bull
OccurrenceNote: This means that instead of worshiping God they worshiped the image of the bull. Alternate translation: “They traded worshiping the glory of God to worship the image of a bull” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the glory of God
OccurrenceNote: Here God is referred to by his glory. Alternate translation: “their glorious God” or “God who is glorious” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the land of Ham
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the land where Ham’s descendants lived. Alternate translation: “the land where Ham’s descendant live” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-possession]])

GLQuote: stood in the breach before him, to turn away his anger from destroying them
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks about Moses persuading Yahweh not to destroy the Israelites as intervening with him in the breach. Alternate translation: “stood between Yahweh and the Israelites and begged Yahweh to not destroy them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: scatter their descendants … in foreign lands
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have basically the same meaning and are used together for emphasis. Alternate translation: “and that he would make their descendants live in foreign lands” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the sacrifices offered to the dead
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the sacrifices that they offered to the dead” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: to the dead
OccurrenceNote: “The dead” refers to the idols and gods that the Israelites were worshiping. Alternate translation: “to gods who are dead” or “to lifeless gods” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: Then Phinehas rose to intervene
OccurrenceNote: Phinehas intervened among the people, punishing them for their sin. This can be made clear. Alternate translation: “Then Phinehas rose to intervene among the people because of their sin” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: It was counted to him as a righteous deed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People credited it to him as a righteous deed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: suffered because of them
OccurrenceNote: Moses suffered because of the peoples’ sin. Here the word “them” is a pronoun for the people and a metonym referring to their sin. Alternate translation: “suffered because of their actions” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: but they mingled with the nations
OccurrenceNote: Hey David speaks of the people intermarrying with the women from other nations as “mingling” with them. Alternate translation: “but they mixed in marriage with the other nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and of their daughters
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “shedding blood” is a descriptive euphemism used for “killing.” Alternate translation: “They shed innocent blood when they killed their sons and daughters” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: They were defiled by their deeds
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Their deeds defiled them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: in their actions they were like prostitutes
OccurrenceNote: Here David compares their unfaithfulness to Yahweh to the unfaithfulness of a prostitute. Alternate translation: “they were as unfaithful to Yahweh as prostitutes” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He gave them into the hand of the nations
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to power or control. Alternate translation: “God allowed the nations to take control of them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: they were brought into subjection to their authority
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “their enemies caused them to be subject to their authority” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: were brought low by their own sin
OccurrenceNote: Here the phrase “brought low” means to be destroyed. Also, If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “their sin ruined them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: called to mind
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “call to mind” means to remember something. Alternate translation: “remembered” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: to your holy name
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh is referred to by his “holy name.” Alternate translation: “to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: May Yahweh, the God of Israel, be praised
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “May people praise Yahweh the God of Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: from everlasting to everlasting
OccurrenceNote: This refers to two extremes and means for all time. See how you translated this in [Psalms 41:13](../041/013.md). Alternate translation: “for all eternity” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: his covenant faithfulness endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “he remains faithful to his covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: the redeemed of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: “The redeemed” refers to the people whom Yahweh has saved. Alternate translation: “those whom Yahweh has saved” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: speak out
OccurrenceNote: This means to tell others about something. Alternate translation: “tell about what Yahweh has done” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: from the hand of the enemy
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to power. Alternate translation: “from the power of the enemy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: from the east … and from the south
OccurrenceNote: Here the four directions are given to emphasize that he gather them from everywhere. Alternate translation: “from every direction” or “from every part of the world” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south
OccurrenceNote: This describes the places that Yahweh gather his people from. Alternate translation: “he has gathered them from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: Then they called out to Yahweh in their trouble
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they are praying to Yahweh so that he will help them. Alternate translation: “Then they prayed to Yahweh to help them in their trouble” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Oh that people would praise Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “Oh” is used to convey a strong desire for people to praise Yahweh. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Let people praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” or “People should praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclamations]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Some sat
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that these are people that Yahweh has rescued. Alternate translation: “Yahweh also rescued people who sat” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: in darkness and in gloom
OccurrenceNote: Both “darkness” and “gloom” have basically the same meaning and are used to emphasize how dark the prison was. Alternate translation: “in complete darkness” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: they had rebelled against God’s word … rejected the instruction of the Most High
OccurrenceNote: These phrases have similar meanings and emphasize how much they had rebelled again God, which is why they had been imprisoned. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: He humbled their hearts through hardship
OccurrenceNote: Here the heart represents a person, but specifically his will. Alternate translation: “He humbled them by allowing them to suffer hardship” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: they stumbled and there was no one to help them up
OccurrenceNote: The word “stumbled” refers to times when these people got into very difficult situations. Alternate translation: “they got into trouble and there was no one to help them out of it” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Then they called out to Yahweh in their trouble
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they are praying to Yahweh so that he will help them. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:6](../107/006.md). Alternate translation: “Then they prayed to Yahweh to help them in their trouble” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: he brought
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes Yahweh saving them from their distress as if their distress were a physical place that he was bringing them out of. Alternate translation: “he saved” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: darkness and gloom
OccurrenceNote: Both “darkness” and “gloom” have basically the same meaning and are used to emphasize how dark the prison was. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:10](../107/010.md). Alternate translation: “complete darkness” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: Oh that people would praise Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “Oh” is used to convey a strong desire for people to praise Yahweh. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:8](../107/008.md). Alternate translation: “Let people praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” or “People should praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclamations]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: For he has broken the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases describe Yahweh freeing his people from prison and are used to emphasize that Yahweh truly freed them. Alternate translation: “He freed his people from prison” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: and afflicted
OccurrenceNote: “and they suffered.” Specifically they were afflicted by becoming sick. Alternate translation: “and they became sick” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: they came close to the gates of death
OccurrenceNote: Here the act of “dying” is described as a place, “the gates of death” Alternate translation: “they almost died” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Then they called out to Yahweh in their trouble
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they are praying to Yahweh so that he will help them. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:6](../107/006.md). Alternate translation: “Then they prayed to Yahweh to help them in their trouble” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He sent his word and healed them
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes Yahweh speaking as sending his words as if they were a messenger. This could mean: (1) “He commanded for them to be healed and they were healed” or (2) “He encouraged them and healed them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Oh that people would praise Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “Oh” is used to convey a strong desire for people to praise Yahweh. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:8](../107/008.md). Alternate translation: “Let people praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” or “People should praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclamations]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: and do business overseas
OccurrenceNote: They would sail to places and buy and sell things with the people there. Alternate translation: “selling things in cities far away” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: that stirs up the seas
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes the winds causing the waves to become high as if the wind was an object fiercely stirring something. Alternate translation: “that caused the waves of the sea to become very high” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: They reached up to the sky; they went down to the depths
OccurrenceNote: This describes the ships rising and falling with the waves. The extremes of rising to the sky and falling to the depths are an exaggeration to express how horrible the windstorm was and how large the waves were. Alternate translation: “their ships would rise very high on the waves and then they would fall very low between the waves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: Their lives melted away in distress
OccurrenceNote: This idiom describes the sailors’ great fear. Alternate translation: “The men were terrified and greatly distressed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: were at their wits’ end
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “at their wit’s end” means that they did not know what to do. Alternate translation: “and they did not know what to do” or “they had no idea what to do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Then they called out to Yahweh in their trouble
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they are praying to Yahweh so that he will help them. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:6](../107/006.md). Alternate translation: “Then they prayed to Yahweh to help them in their trouble” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the waves were stilled
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “he made the waves still” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Oh that people would praise Yahweh for his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “Oh” is used to convey a strong desire for people to praise Yahweh. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. See how you translated this in [Psalms 107:8](../107/008.md). Alternate translation: “Let people praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” or “People should praise Yahweh because he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclamations]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: He turns the wilderness into a pool of water and dry land into springs of water
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases have similar meaning and emphasize how Yahweh makes water appear in the wilderness. Alternate translation: “He make springs and lakes in land that used to be desert” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: He settles the hungry there
OccurrenceNote: The word “there” refers to the places where Yahweh made springs and lakes appear. Also, the phrase “the hungry” refers to people who are hungry. Alternate translation: “Yahweh makes people who are hungry live there” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: He does not let their cattle decrease in number
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated in positive form. Alternate translation: “He keeps their cattle very numerous” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]])

GLQuote: They were diminished and brought low
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Their leaders diminished their number and brought them low” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: brought low
OccurrenceNote: This means to be humiliated. Alternate translation: “humiliated” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: pours contempt on
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks of Yahweh showing contempt for the leaders as if contempt were a liquid he poured out on them. Alternate translation: “shows contempt for” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the leaders
OccurrenceNote: “the nobles.” This refers to the leaders who oppressed the people. Alternate translation: “the leaders who oppressed them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the needy
OccurrenceNote: This refers to needy people. Alternate translation: “needy people” or “poor people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: cares for his families like a flock
OccurrenceNote: Here David compares how Yahweh cares for his people to how a shepherd cares for his sheep. This could mean: (1) “makes the number of people in their families increase like flocks” or (2) “takes care of them like a shepherd cares for his sheep” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: The upright
OccurrenceNote: This refers to people who live in an upright way. Alternate translation: “Upright people” or “People who do what is right” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: all wickedness
OccurrenceNote: Here wicked people are referred to as “wickedness.” Alternate translation: “all wicked people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: shuts its mouth
OccurrenceNote: This means to not say anything in response. Alternate translation: “has nothing to say against Yahweh in reply” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: take note of these things
OccurrenceNote: This means to think about these things. Alternate translation: “think about these things” or “remember these things” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: meditate on Yahweh’s acts of covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “meditate on the things that Yahweh has done that show that he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: My heart is fixed, God
OccurrenceNote: Here David is referring to himself by his heart. Also, the word “fixed” means to trust completely. Alternate translation: “My heart is fixed on you, God” or “I am trusting completely in you, God” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: I will sing praises also with my honored heart
OccurrenceNote: Here David is represented by his “heart.” David refers to himself as having the honor of praising God. Alternate translation: “You honor me by allowing me to sing praises to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Wake up, lute and harp
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes playing his instruments as waking them up from sleep. Alternate translation: “I will praise you by playing the lute and the harp” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: I will wake up the dawn
OccurrenceNote: Here David is describing the dawn waking up like a person waking up in the morning. Alternate translation: “I will be praising you when the dawn comes” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: your covenant faithfulness is great above the heavens; and your trustworthiness reaches to the skies
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings. They speak of the greatness of Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness as if they were objects that were tall enough to reach up to the sky. The abstract nouns “faithfulness” and “trustworthiness” can be translated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “For your covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness are greater than the distance between heaven and earth” or “For you are more faithful to your covenant and more worthy of people trusting you than the sky is higher than the earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Be exalted, God, above the heavens
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist is asking God to show that he is exalted. Being exalted above the heavens represents being great. Alternate translation: “God, show that you are exalted above the heavens” or “God, show that you are great in the heavens” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: may your glory be exalted
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh is referred to by his “glory.” Alternate translation: “may you be exalted” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: So that those you love may be rescued
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: Because those you love need rescuing” or “Rescue those you love” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: with your right hand
OccurrenceNote: Here Yahweh’s “right hand” refers to his power. Alternate translation: “by your power” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: answer me
OccurrenceNote: Answering here represents responding to his request. Alternate translation: “respond to my request” or “answer my prayer” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: God has spoken in his holiness
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes God speaking something because he is holy as speaking “in his holiness,” as if his holiness were something that he was physically inside of. Alternate translation: “God, because he is holy, has said” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Ephraim also is my helmet
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of the tribe of Ephraim as if it were his army. The helmet symbolizes equipment for war. Alternate translation: “Ephraim is like a helmet I have chosen” or “The tribe of Ephraim is my army” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Judah is my scepter
OccurrenceNote: God chose men from the tribe of Judah to be the kings of his people, and he speaks of that tribe as if it were his scepter. Alternate translation: “The tribe of Judah is like my scepter” or “Judah is the tribe through whom I rule my people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Moab is my washbasin
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Moab being unimportant as if Moab were a washbasin or a lowly servant. Alternate translation: “Moab is like a bowl that I use for washing” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: over Edom I will throw my shoe
OccurrenceNote: God was probably speaking of taking ownership of Edom as if he were symbolically throwing his shoe onto that land to show that he owns it. However some versions have other interpretations. Alternate translation: “I take ownership of the land of Edom” or “I throw my shoe onto the land of Edom to show that it is mine” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-symaction]])

GLQuote: God, have you not rejected us?
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist uses this question to express his sadness that it seems that God has rejected them. Alternate translation: “It seems like you have rejected us!” or “God, you seem to have abandoned us!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: You do not go into battle with our army
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of God helping their army as if God were to go and fight with them. Alternate translation: “you do not help our army when we go into battle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he will trample down our enemies
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of God helping their army defeat their enemies as if God were to trample down the enemies. Alternate translation: “he will enable us to trample down our enemies” or “he will make us able to defeat our enemies. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: For the wicked and deceitful
OccurrenceNote: The words “wicked” and “deceitful” refer to people. They have similar meanings and emphasize how bad these people are. Alternate translation: “For wicked and deceitful men” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: they accuse me
OccurrenceNote: The word “they” refers to the people who are wicked and deceitful. You may need to make explicit that those who accuse the psalmist do so falsely. Alternate translation: “they accuse me falsely” or “they slander me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Appoint a wicked man … appoint an accuser
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases are parallel and the phrases “a wicked man” and “an accuser” refer to the same person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: When he is judged, may he be found guilty
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “When he is on trial, may the judge find him guilty” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: may his prayer be considered sinful
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “consider his prayer sinful” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: May his days be few
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “his days” refers to the length of his life. Alternate translation: “May he not live a long time” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: May his children be cut off; may their name be blotted out
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have similar meanings and emphasize his children being destroyed. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: May his children be cut off
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Cause his children to be cut off” or “Cause his children to die” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: may their name be blotted out in the next generation
OccurrenceNote: Here the idea of there being no one to carry on the family name is spoke of as “their name being blotted out.” Alternate translation: “may there be no one to carry on his name” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: May his ancestors’ sins be mentioned to Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “May you remember the sins of his ancestors, Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: may the sin of his mother not be forgotten
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “May you not forget the sins that his mother committed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: May their guilt always be before Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks about Yahweh thinking about their guilt as if their guilt is something physically present before him. Alternate translation: “May Yahweh continually think about their sins” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: may Yahweh cut off their memory from the earth
OccurrenceNote: David uses the word “earth” to refer to all the people that live on the earth. Also, the phrase “their memory” refers to people remembering them after they have died. Alternate translation: “may Yahweh make it so that no one on earth remembers them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: this man never bothered to show any covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: This refers to him showing covenant faithfulness to people. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “this man never bothered to show any covenant faithfulness to people” or “this man never did anything to show that he was faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: the oppressed, the needy
OccurrenceNote: This refers to oppressed and needy people. Alternate translation: “oppressed people, needy people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: the disheartened
OccurrenceNote: This refers to people who are disheartened. Alternate translation: “disheartened people” or “people who have lost hope” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: He clothed himself with cursing as his garment
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of the wicked person’s behavior as if it were his clothing. Alternate translation: “He cursed other people as often as he wore clothing” or “He cursed people all the time” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: his curse came into his inner being like water, like oil into his bones
OccurrenceNote: Possible meanings are: (1) He spoke curses so often that they became a part of his identity. “the curses that he speaks are part of who he is” or (2) the curse that he spoke happened to him. “his whole being was cursed by the curse he spoke” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: like water
OccurrenceNote: This refers to how a person drinks water. Alternate translation: “like water a person drinks” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: like oil into his bones
OccurrenceNote: This refers to how oil soaks into bones when rubbed on the skin. Alternate translation: “like olive oil soaks into a person’s bones when it is rubbed on his skin” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: May his curses be to him like the clothes he wears to cover himself
OccurrenceNote: People wore their clothes everyday. David speaks of a wicked person always being cursed as if his curses always covered him as his clothing does. Alternate translation: “Let his curses be on him every day like the garment he wears” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: like the belt he always wears
OccurrenceNote: The words “may his curses be to him” are understood from the previous phrase. They may be repeated here. Alternate translation: “may his curses be to him like the belt he always wears” or “and let his curses always be on him like the belt he always wears” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: deal kindly with me
OccurrenceNote: This is a request for Yahweh to treat him kindly. Alternate translation: “treat me kindly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Because your covenant faithfulness is good
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Because you are good and are faithful to your covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: oppressed and needy
OccurrenceNote: These two words have similar meanings and emphasize that he is unable to help himself. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: my heart is wounded within me
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks of being in great despair as his heart being wounded. Alternate translation: “I am full of grief and despair” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I am fading away like the shadow … like a locust
OccurrenceNote: David feels like he is going to die soon and describes this feeling by comparing himself to a fading shadow and to how the wind blows away locust. Alternate translation: “I feel like I am about to die, like an evening shadow that will soon disappear, like a locust is easily blown away by the wind” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: My knees are weak
OccurrenceNote: This means that he is weak and it is difficult for him to stand. Alternate translation: “I have difficulty standing” or “My body is weak” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: I am turning to skin and bones
OccurrenceNote: This means that he has lost a lot of weight. Alternate translation: “my body has become very thin” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: I am disdained by my accusers
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “My accusers ridicule me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: save me by your covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “save me because you are faithful to your covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: may they be put to shame
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “may they be ashamed” or “let them be ashamed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: May my adversaries be clothed … may they wear
OccurrenceNote: These two phrase have them same meaning and are used together for emphasize how greatly he wishes for them to be ashamed. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: be clothed with shame
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks of them being ashamed as if were clothing they wore. Alternate translation: “be very ashamed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: may they wear their shame like a robe
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of them being ashamed as if it were a robe that they wore. Alternate translation: “may their shame cover them just like their robe is wrapped around them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: With my mouth I give
OccurrenceNote: This means that he will speak. Alternate translation: “I will speak and give” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: will stand at the right hand of the one who is needy
OccurrenceNote: This means that he will help and defend the poor person. Alternate translation: “will defend the one who is needy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Sit at my right hand
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “my right hand” refers to the place of honor. Alternate translation: “Sit at the place of honor which I have for you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: make your enemies your footstool
OccurrenceNote: Here David describes Yahweh placing his master’s enemies under his power and control as putting them under his feet like a footstool. Alternate translation: “put your enemies under your power” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Yahweh will hold out the scepter of your strength
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks of Yahweh extending the area that the king rules as holding out his scepter. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will extend the area over which you powerfully rule” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: on the day of your power
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the day that the king will lead his armies into battle. This can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “on the day that you lead your armies into battle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: from the womb of the dawn … like the dew
OccurrenceNote: David describes the dew as a baby to whom the dawn gives birth. Alternate translation: “in the morning … like the dew” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: from the womb of the dawn your youth will be to you like the dew
OccurrenceNote: David is telling the king that he will have youthful strength each morning by comparing it to how the dew appears early each morning. Alternate translation: “each morning you will be filled with youthful strength to sustain you just like each morning the dew appears to water and sustain the earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: will not change
OccurrenceNote: This means that he will not change what he has said. Alternate translation: “will not change his mind” or “will not change what he has said” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: after the manner of Melchizedek
OccurrenceNote: The idea of being priest is understood from the previous phrase. It can be stated clearly here. Alternate translation: “after the manner that Melchizedek was priest” or “in the same way that Melchizedek was priest” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: The Lord is at your right hand
OccurrenceNote: When the lord goes to battle, Yahweh stands at his right hand in order to help him. Alternate translation: “The Lord helps you in battle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: He will kill
OccurrenceNote: The word “He” refers to Yahweh. He will cause the kings to be defeated and die, but he will allow the king’s armies to kill the enemy kings. Alternate translation: “He will cause the kings to die” or “He will allow your armies to kill the kings” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: kings
OccurrenceNote: This refers to his enemies. Alternate translation: “enemy kings” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: on the day of his anger
OccurrenceNote: Here David speaks of the day when Yahweh will become angry and defeat the kings as “the day of his anger.” Alternate translation: “on the day of judgment when his patience turns to anger” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: he will fill the battlegrounds with dead bodies
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh will cause this to happen, not that he will personally kill all of the people who die on the battleground. Alternate translation: “he will cause the battlegrounds to be filled with death bodies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: he will kill the leaders in many countries
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh will cause this to happen, not that he will personally kill the leaders. Alternate translation: “he will cause the leaders in many countries to be killed” or “he will allow the leaders in many countries to die” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: He will drink of the brook along the road
OccurrenceNote: The king only stops briefly for a drink and then he continues the pursuit of his enemies. Alternate translation: “As he pursues his enemies, he will only stop to drink quickly from a brook” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: of the brook
OccurrenceNote: This means the he will drink water from the brook. A brook is a small stream. Alternate translation: “he will drink water from the brook” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: he will lift his head up high after victory
OccurrenceNote: People raised their heads when they are victorious, confident, and joyful. Alternate translation: “he will confidently lift his head after victory” or “he will be victorious” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: with my whole heart
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “heart” represents the person’s entire inner being and emotions. Alternate translation: “with all that I am” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: in the assembly of the upright, in their gathering
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean that same thing and may be combined if necessary. Alternate translation: “in the gathering of upright people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: eagerly awaited by all those who desire them
OccurrenceNote: The word “them” refers to the “works of Yahweh.” If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “all those who desire the works of Yahweh eagerly await them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: that will be remembered
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “that people will always remember” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: call to mind
OccurrenceNote: This is an idiom that means to remember. Alternate translation: “remember” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the inheritance of the nations
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of the land that belonged to the nations in Canaan as if it were their inheritance. Alternate translation: “the land that belonged to other nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: The works of his hands
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “hands” refers to Yahweh, himself. Alternate translation: “The works that he does” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: They are established forever
OccurrenceNote: This means that Yahweh’s instructions are unchangeable and will last forever. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “He has established them forever” or “They will last forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: to be observed faithfully and properly
