OccurrenceNote: Here “feet” refers to the whole person. Alternate translation: “we are standing” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: within your gates
OccurrenceNote: Here “gates” refers to the city. Alternate translation: “inside you, Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: the name of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Here “name” refers to Yahweh himself. Alternate translation: “Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the house of David
OccurrenceNote: Here “house” refers to the descendants of David. Alternate translation: “the descendants of David” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: May those who love you have peace
OccurrenceNote: This section states the content of the prayer that the writer wants his audience to pray. He asks them to speak directly to the city of Jerusalem, as if the city was a person who could hear them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

This verse finishes the prayer that the writer wants his audience to pray. He asks them to speak directly to the city of Jerusalem, as if the city was a person who could hear them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: May there be peace within … may they have peace within
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases have the same meanings and are used together to strengthen each other. Alternate translation: “May the people in Jerusalem live in peace” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: within the walls that defend you … within your fortresses
OccurrenceNote: Here Jerusalem is referred to by the fortress walls that protects it. The terms “walls” and “fortress” refer to the same thing. Alternate translation: “within Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: General Information:
OccurrenceNote: In this section, the writer speaks directly to the city of Jerusalem, as if the city was a person who could hear them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: I lift up my eyes
OccurrenceNote: Here the author refers to his eyes because that is the part of the body used for seeing. Alternate translation: “I look to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: as the eyes of servants … as the eyes of a maid … so our eyes look
OccurrenceNote: These three phrases have similar meanings. The third phrase, about the Israelites, is being compared to how the servants and maids look to their masters and mistresses for help. In each case “eyes” refers to the whole person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: master’s hand … mistress’s hand
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to the provision for needs. Alternate translation: “master’s provision … mistress’s provision” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: has mercy on us
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **mercy**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: “act mercifully toward us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Have mercy on us
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **mercy**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. See how you translated a similar phrase in [Psalms 123:2](../123/002.md). Alternate translation: “act mercifully toward us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: we are filled with humiliation
OccurrenceNote: Here humiliation is spoken of as if it were something that could be fill up a person. “we are very disgraced” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: We are more than full
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means that the amount is excessive, in a negative sense. Alternate translation: “We have had too much” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: of the scoffing … and with the contempt
OccurrenceNote: There two phrases have very similar meanings and are used together to emphasize how much they have been mocked by the people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the insolent
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the insolent people. Alternate translation: “rude and arrogant people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: the proud
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the proud people. Alternate translation: “the people who are proud” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: “If Yahweh had not been on our side
OccurrenceNote: This is the beginning of a hypothetical statement about something that did not actually happen. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: if it had not been Yahweh who was on our side
OccurrenceNote: This is the continuation of a hypothetical statement about something that did not actually happen. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: then they would have swallowed us up alive
OccurrenceNote: This is the end of a hypothetical statement that begins with the words “If Yahweh had not been on our side” in [Psalms 124:1](../124/001.md) and continues with the words “if it had not been Yahweh who was on our side when men rose up against us” in [Psalms 124:2](./002.md). It describes a result that did not happen because Yahweh was actually on their side. “They were not able to swallow us up alive because Yahweh was on our side.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: swallowed us up alive
OccurrenceNote: This metaphor describes how the Israelites could have died to how a fierce animal would attack a smaller animal to eat. Alternate translation: “killed us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: their anger raged against us
OccurrenceNote: Here “their anger” refers to the enemies who were angry. Alternate translation: “they were very angry with us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: The water would have swept us away; the torrent would have overwhelmed us
OccurrenceNote: This is the end of a hypothetical statement that begins with the words “If Yahweh had not been on our side” in [Psalms 124:1](../124/001.md) and continues with the words “if it had not been Yahweh who was on our side when men rose up against us” in [Psalms 124:2](./002.md). It describes a result that did not happen because Yahweh was actually on their side. “The water did not sweep us away, and the torrent did not overwhelm us because Yahweh was on our side” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: The water would have swept us away
OccurrenceNote: Here the enemies of the writer are spoken of as if they were a flood of water. Alternate translation: “Our enemies would have easily defeated us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the torrent would have overwhelmed us
OccurrenceNote: Here the enemies of the writer are spoken of as if they were a flood of water that would have drowned the Israelites. Alternate translation: “our enemies would have overwhelmed us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Then the raging waters would have drowned us
OccurrenceNote: This is the end of a hypothetical statement that begins with the words “If Yahweh had not been on our side” in [Psalms 124:1](../124/001.md) and continues with the words “if it had not been Yahweh who was on our side when men rose up against us” in [Psalms 124:2](./002.md). It describes a result that did not happen because Yahweh was actually on their side. “The raging waters did not drown us because Yahweh was on our side” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: the raging waters would have drowned us
OccurrenceNote: Here the enemies of the writer are spoken of as if they were a raging river that would have drowned the Israelites. Alternate translation: “our enemies would have destroyed us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: torn by their teeth
OccurrenceNote: The enemies are spoken of as if they were wild animals that would destroy the Israelites by eating them. Alternate translation: “destroyed as if we were eaten by wild animals” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: escaped like a bird out of the snare of the fowlers
OccurrenceNote: The writer describes his escape from the enemies as if he was a bird that had escaped from the snare of the hunters. Alternate translation: “escaped from our enemies as a bird escapes from the trap that hunters have set” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the snare has been broken
OccurrenceNote: The plot of the enemies to catch the writer failed as if it was a snare that had broken. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Those who trust in Yahweh are like Mount Zion, unshakable, forever enduring
OccurrenceNote: People who trust in Yahweh are spoken of as if they were Mount Zion. Mountains are unable to be moved. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so Yahweh surrounds his people
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s protection is spoken of as if he was the mountains surrounding Jerusalem. Jerusalem was surrounded by several mountains, which protected it from attack. Alternate translation: “As the hills that surround Jerusalem protect it, so Yahweh protects his people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: now and forever
OccurrenceNote: Here, this phrase means “always.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: The scepter of wickedness
OccurrenceNote: Here the scepter of wickedness represents the rule of wicked people. Alternate translation: “Wicked people” or “Wicked rulers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: are upright in their hearts
OccurrenceNote: Here, “hearts” refers to their desires. Alternate translation: “desire to do the right” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: turn aside
OccurrenceNote: Refusing to obey Yahweh is spoken of as turning away from a good path. Alternate translation: “leave good and go” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: their crooked ways
OccurrenceNote: Here wicked ways are spoken of as if they were a path that is not straight. Alternate translation: “their wicked ways” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: lead them away
OccurrenceNote: People are lead away in order to punish them. The full meaning of this statement can be made clear. Alternate translation: “lead them away to punish them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: our mouths were filled with laughter
OccurrenceNote: Laughing is spoken of as if their mouths were a container and their laughter was in it. It can be made clear that this laughter was a response to their joy. Alternate translation: “we laughed for joy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: our tongues with singing
OccurrenceNote: The verbs “were filled” can be stated clearly. Singing is spoken of as if their tongues were containers and singing was in them. Alternate translation: “our tongues were filled with singing” or “we sang songs of joy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: eat the bread of hard work
OccurrenceNote: This is an idiom. Bread often represents the food a person needs every day in order to live. Alternate translation: “work hard for your daily needs” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: heritage
OccurrenceNote: property that a person can inherit from his ancestors. Children normally receive an inheritance from their parents. Inheritance goes from parents to children. This passage uses parents inheriting children from Yahweh as a metaphor for Yahweh being the only one who can give children. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are the children of one’s youth
OccurrenceNote: Arrows are very important to a warrior because they protect him in battle. Children are spoken of as if they are a warrior’s arrow. Alternate translation: “Having many children will help to protect you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: his quiver full of them
OccurrenceNote: A quiver is a container for arrows. Having many children is spoken of as if the children were arrows in a quiver. Alternate translation: “a home full of children” or “many children” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Blessed is everyone who honors Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: This phrase occurs in the passive voice to avoid implying that Yahweh is obligated to bless those who honor him. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will bless everyone who honors him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: What your hands provide
OccurrenceNote: A man can be referred to by his hands because that is the part of the body he works with. Alternate translation: “What you provide” or “What you work for” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: you will be blessed and prosper
OccurrenceNote: The words “be blessed” and “prosper” share similar meanings and emphasize God’s favor. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will bless you and prosper you” or “Yahweh will make you blessed and prosperous” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: like a fruitful vine in your house
OccurrenceNote: The wife is spoke of as a vine producing a lot of fruit. This implies that children are like fruit and the wife will have many children. Alternate translation: “very productive and give you many children” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: your children will be like olive plants
OccurrenceNote: Children are compared to olive plants because of the way they grow to surround something. Children will surround the table and make it full. Alternate translation: “you will have many children who will grow and prosper” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: the man will be blessed who honors Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated as an active verb. “Yahweh will bless the man who honors him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: The plowers plowed on my back
OccurrenceNote: The cuts from a whipping are spoken of as the plow of a plowman. A farmer plowed deep lines into a field. Alternate translation: “My enemies have cut me deeply on my back” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: they made their furrows long
OccurrenceNote: This is a continuation of the plowing metaphor. The “furrow” is the line the farmer plowed. Alternate translation: “they made their cuts long” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he has cut the ropes of the wicked
OccurrenceNote: Israel is spoken of as being bound by evil people. Alternate translation: “he has freed us from our enemies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: May they all be put to shame and turned back
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh is not explicitly mentioned as the one who does these things. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “May Yahweh shame them and defeat them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: May they be like the grass on the housetops that withers before it grows up
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of his enemies dying and being few in number. He compares them to the little bit of grass that grows on the roof of a house and withers and is not enough to cut or bundle. Alternate translation: “May they die and may there be few of them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: that cannot fill … together
OccurrenceNote: These words finish the simile that begins in ([Psalms 129:6](../129/006.md)). The psalmist speaks of his enemies dying and being few in number. He compares them to the little bit of grass that grows on the roof of a house and withers and is not enough to cut or bundle. “May they be like the grass, which cannot fill … together” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: Out of the depths I
OccurrenceNote: The author’s sadness is spoken of as if it were a container. His sadness comes from the bottom of the container. Sadness is often spoken of as being a container that fills from the top to the bottom. Alternate translation: “Because I am very sad, I” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: let your ears be attentive
OccurrenceNote: The ears represent Yahweh, but because the author knows that Yahweh hears everything, he is really asking for Yahweh to respond. Alternate translation: “please listen” or “please respond” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: to my pleas for mercy
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **mercy**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “merciful.” Alternate translation: “to my pleas and be merciful to me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: who could stand?
OccurrenceNote: The speaker uses this question to express the futility of thinking that anyone could stand in this situation. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “no one could stand.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: who could stand
OccurrenceNote: “Stand” often represents escaping or surviving when someone attacks. In this case, it would be to escape from being punished. Alternate translation: “no one could escape from your punishment” or “no one could survive your punishment” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: My soul
OccurrenceNote: “My soul” represents the psalmist. Alternate translation: “I” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: My soul waits
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist is spoken of as if he were waiting on something with expectation. Alternate translation: “I hope” or “I trust” or “I desire for something” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: My soul waits … more than watchmen wait for the morning
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of his desire for the Lord to help him as being greater than the desire that those who work all night have for the morning to come. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: Israel, hope in Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: The people of Israel are spoken of as if they were a man. Alternate translation: “You people of Israel, hope in Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: who will redeem Israel from all his sins
OccurrenceNote: The people of Israel are spoken of as if they were a man. Alternate translation: “who will redeem the people of Israel from all their sins” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my heart is not proud or my eyes haughty
OccurrenceNote: The heart and the eyes represent the person. Alternate translation: “I am not proud or haughty” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: things that are beyond me
OccurrenceNote: Things that are too hard for a person to understand are spoken of as if they are beyond the person or too far away from the person to be able to reach them. Alternate translation: “things that are too hard to understand” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I have stilled and quieted my soul
OccurrenceNote: The soul represents the person or his emotions. Being calm and peaceful is spoken of has having making one’s soul still and quiet. Alternate translation: “I am calm and peaceful” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my soul within me
OccurrenceNote: The soul represents the person or his emotions. Alternate translation: “I” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: a weaned child with his mother
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of himself being content and resting as if he were a young child that no longer demands breast milk from his mother. Alternate translation: “content like a young child that no longer cries for breast milk but rests in his mother’s arms” or “content and resting” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will not give sleep to my eyes or rest to my eyelids
OccurrenceNote: Sleep and rest are spoken of as if they are things that can be given. Here eyes and eyelids represent the whole person. Alternate translation: “I will not allow my eyes to sleep or my eyelids to rest” or “I will not sleep or close my eyes and rest” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: until I find a place for Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Building a place for Yahweh is spoken of as finding a place for him. Alternate translation: “until I build a place for Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: we heard about it in Ephrathah
OccurrenceNote: The word “it” probably refers to where God’s sacred chest was. The phrase “in Ephrathah” probably refers to where they were when they heard about it. This can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “we who were in Ephrathah heard about where the sacred chest was” or “we in Ephrathah heard that the holy box was in Jaar” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: we will worship at his footstool
OccurrenceNote: Worshiping God at the covenant box is spoken of as bowing at the feet of the king who is sitting on his throne. This communicates humility and submission to God. Alternate translation: “we will go to God’s covenant box and worship him as king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Arise, Yahweh, to your resting place
OccurrenceNote: The verb “come” can be stated clearly. “Arise, Yahweh, and come to your resting place” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: your resting place
OccurrenceNote: The place God chose for people to worship him is spoken of as if it were a place where he rests or lives eternally. Alternate translation: “the place where you stay” or “your tabernacle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you and the ark of your strength!
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “come to the ark of your strength” or (2) “come, and make the ark of your strength come.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: May your priests be clothed with integrity
OccurrenceNote: Integrity is spoken of as if it were clothing. Alternate translation: “May people recognize that your priests have integrity” or “I want people see how your priests always do what is right” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: do not turn away from your anointed king
OccurrenceNote: Here “turning away” means to reject someone. Alternate translation: “do not abandon the king that you anointed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will place one of your descendants on your throne
OccurrenceNote: Making a king’s descendant become king in his place is spoken of as placing him on that king’s throne. AT “I will cause one of your descendants to rule Israel in your place” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: sit on your throne
OccurrenceNote: Ruling as king is spoken of as sitting on the throne. Alternate translation: “rule as king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: your sons
OccurrenceNote: Here “your sons” represents the descendants of David that would become king. Alternate translation: “your descendants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: General Information:
OccurrenceNote: “He”, “my” and “I” refer to Yahweh and “her” refers to Zion. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-pronouns]])

GLQuote: Zion … her
OccurrenceNote: The author writes as though the city of Zion were a woman. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: he has desired her for his seat
OccurrenceNote: “Yahweh has desired Zion for Yahweh’s seat.” Here, **seat** could mean: (1) his throne where he would rule, or (2) the place where he would stay. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: her
OccurrenceNote: The author writes as though the city of Zion ([Psalms 132:13](../132/013.md)) were a woman. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: my resting place
OccurrenceNote: The place God chose for people to worship him is spoken of as if it were a place where he rests or lives eternally. Alternate translation: “the place where I stay” or “my tabernacle” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])
God continues to speak about the city of Zion as if Zion was a woman. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: will satisfy her poor with bread
OccurrenceNote: Here “poor” refers to the poor people in Zion and “bread” probably represents food in general. Alternate translation: “will satisfy the poor people in Zion with food” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: I will clothe her priests with salvation
OccurrenceNote: Salvation is spoken of as if it is clothing. This could mean: (1) “I will cause the priests to behave in a manner worthy of ones whom I have saved” or (2) “I will save her priests” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will make a horn to sprout for David
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of a powerful descendant of David as if he was the powerful horn of an animal. Alternate translation: “I will make a descendant of David become king after him” or “I will cause David to have a descendant who will be a powerful king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: set up a lamp for my anointed one
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of causing David’s descendants to continue to rule as king as if they were a lamp that would continue to shine. Alternate translation: “I will cause my anointed one’s descendants to continue to rule as king” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will clothe his enemies with shame
OccurrenceNote: Shame is spoken of as if it was clothing. This shame would result from losing in war. Alternate translation: “I will cause his enemies to be ashamed” or “I will cause his enemies to be defeated and ashamed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: his crown will shine
OccurrenceNote: The crown represents his rule, and greatness is spoken of as shining. Alternate translation: “he will be a great king” or “his greatness will shine” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: for brothers to live together
OccurrenceNote: The relationships among fellow God’s people is spoken of as if they were brothers. Alternate translation: “for God’s people to live together peacefully as brothers” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: It is like fine oil on the head
OccurrenceNote: The goodness of unity among God’s people is spoken of as if it were like the fine oil that was poured on Aaron’s head. Alternate translation: “This unity is precious like the oil that was poured on Aaron’s head” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: like the dew of Hermon
OccurrenceNote: The goodness of unity among God’s people is spoken of as it if it were refreshing like dew. Alternate translation: “refreshing like the dew of Hermon” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: heaven and earth
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “heaven and earth” here represents all things. Alternate translation: “everything in heaven and earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: Praise the name of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s name represents him. “Praise Yahweh” or “Praise him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: stand in Yahweh’s house
OccurrenceNote: This represents serving Yahweh in his temple. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Yahweh has chosen Jacob
OccurrenceNote: “Jacob” here refers to his descendants, the people of Israel. Alternate translation: “Yahweh has chosen Jacob’s descendants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Israel as his possession
OccurrenceNote: The beginning of the sentence can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “he has chosen Israel to be his possession” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: that our Lord is above all gods
OccurrenceNote: “I know that our Lord is above all gods.” Being greater than something is spoken of as being above it. Alternate translation: “that our Lord is greater than all gods” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: bringing the wind out of his storehouse
OccurrenceNote: A storehouse is a place where things are kept for future use. This imagery shows God’s power to control the wind. Alternate translation: “causing the wind to blow by his power” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: signs and wonders
OccurrenceNote: These two words mean basically the same thing and refer to the miraculous troubles that God had caused in Egypt. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: into your midst, Egypt
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks as if the people of Egypt were listening to him. Alternate translation: “among you people of Egypt” or “among the people of Egypt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]])

GLQuote: He gave us their land as an inheritance
OccurrenceNote: God’s gift of the land to the Israelites is spoken of as if it were inheritance from father to son. Alternate translation: “He gave us their land to have forever” or “He gave us their land to be ours forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Your name
OccurrenceNote: His name here represents his fame or reputation. Alternate translation: “Your fame” or “Your reputation” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Those who make them are like them
OccurrenceNote: Being ignorant and powerless is spoken of as being like idols, which cannot speak, see, hear, or breathe. Alternate translation: “Those who make them are stupid and powerless like their idols” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: he who lives in Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: God is spoken of as if he lived in Jerusalem because the temple where the Israelites worshiped him was there. Alternate translation: “he whose temple is in Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Oh
OccurrenceNote: This is an exclamation that should be translated with whatever exclamation of emphasis you have in your language to make it sound natural. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclamations]])

GLQuote: for his covenant faithfulness endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “because he remains faithful to his covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: the God of gods
OccurrenceNote: the God who is greater than the gods that other people worship (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: to rule by day
OccurrenceNote: The sun is spoken of as if it were a king. Alternate translation: “to mark the time of day” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: for his covenant faithfulness endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. See how you translated this in [Psalms 136:1](../136/001.md). Alternate translation: “because he remains faithful to his covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: to rule by night
OccurrenceNote: The moon, and stars are spoken of as if they were kings. Alternate translation: “to mark the time of night” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: with a strong hand and a raised arm
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” and “arm” represent power. Alternate translation: “with great power” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: overthrew Pharaoh
OccurrenceNote: Here defeat is spoken of as if it were tipping someone over. Alternate translation: “defeated Pharaoh” or “defeated the king of Egypt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Pharaoh
OccurrenceNote: That is, the army of Pharaoh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: helped us in our humiliation
OccurrenceNote: The condition of feeling shame is spoken of as if it were a place that the Israelites had been in. This is a reference to the many times when the Israelites’ enemies had defeated them in battle and shamed them. Alternate translation: “cared when we were shamed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: has given us victory over our enemies
OccurrenceNote: Causing people to be victorious and defeat their enemies is spoken of as giving them victory, as if victory were an object that can be given. Alternate translation: “has made us victorious over our enemies” or “has made us able to defeat our enemies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: we sat … wept … we thought
OccurrenceNote: The writer does not include the readers. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclusive]])

GLQuote: we hung
OccurrenceNote: The writer does not include the readers. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclusive]])

GLQuote: On the poplars there
OccurrenceNote: Poplar trees do not grow in Israel. “Poplars” may here stand for all the trees in Babylon. Alternate translation: “On the trees in Babylon” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: If I ignore the memory of you, Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks as if Jerusalem is listening to him. Alternate translation: “If I act as if I did not remember you, Jerusalem” or “If I try to forget you, Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]])

GLQuote: Call to mind, Yahweh, what the Edomites did
OccurrenceNote: Here remembering what the Edomites did represents punishing them for what they did. Alternate translation: “Punish the Edomites, Yahweh, for what they did” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the day Jerusalem fell
OccurrenceNote: Jerusalem being captured by an enemy army is spoken of as if it had fallen. Who captured Jerusalem can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “the day Jerusalem was captured” or “the day the Babylonian army entered Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: General Information:
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist addresses the people of Babylon as if they were there listening to him. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]])

GLQuote: Daughter of Babylon
OccurrenceNote: This represents the city of Babylon and its people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: may the person be blessed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “may God bless the person” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: pays you back for what you have done to us
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of someone doing to others what they have done as if were payment. Alternate translation: “does to you what you did to us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will give you thanks with my whole heart
OccurrenceNote: The heart here represents the emotions. Doing something sincerely or completely is spoken of as doing it with all one’s heart. Alternate translation: “I will sincerely thank you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: give thanks to your name
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “name” represents Yahweh himself. Alternate translation: “give thanks to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: for your covenant faithfulness and for your trustworthiness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **trustworthiness**, you could express the same idea with a verbal phrase. Alternate translation: “because you are faithful to your covenant and you are worthy of people trusting you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: your name
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “yourself” or (2) “your fame.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: your mouth
OccurrenceNote: This expression stands for God himself. Alternate translation: “you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: the proud he knows from far off
OccurrenceNote: This expression probably means that God is not faithful to those who are proud. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: in the middle of danger
OccurrenceNote: Being in danger is spoken of as being in a physical place. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you will reach out with your hand against the anger of my enemies
OccurrenceNote: God is spoken of as if he will strike the enemies with his hand. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: anger of my enemies
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **anger**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “angry.” Alternate translation: “my enemies, who are angry” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: your covenant faithfulness, Yahweh, endures forever
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “you, Yahweh, remain faithful to your covenant forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: your hands have made
OccurrenceNote: God is spoken of as if he had physically used hands to create. Alternate translation: “you have created” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: when I sit down and when I get up
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist uses these two actions to represent everything he does. Alternate translation: “everything I do” or “everything about me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: my path and my lying down
OccurrenceNote: Here “path” stands for one’s behavior. “My path and my lying down” together represent everything about the psalmist. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: before there is a word on my tongue
OccurrenceNote: Here “word on the tongue” represents speech. Alternate translation: “before I say anything” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: place your hand upon me
OccurrenceNote: This expression refers to guidance and help. Alternate translation: “you guide and help me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: it is too high, and I cannot reach it
OccurrenceNote: Being high and out of reach is an expression, in this case, about some knowledge that human beings cannot have. Alternate translation: “it is too difficult to understand” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Where can I go from your Spirit?…Where can I flee from your presence?
OccurrenceNote: These two questions are in parallel. The psalmist says that he cannot go away from God’s presence. Alternate translation: “I cannot escape from your Spirit.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: if I make my bed in Sheol
OccurrenceNote: “Making one’s bed” refers to staying somewhere. Alternate translation: “even if I stay in Sheol” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: If I fly away on the wings of the morning and go to live in the uttermost parts across the sea
OccurrenceNote: The author uses exaggeration to explain that wherever he is, God is there too. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: If I fly away on the wings of the morning
OccurrenceNote: In the ancient near east, the sun was often imagined as if it had wings which enabled it to fly across the sky. Alternate translation: “If the sun could carry me with itself across the sky” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: If I said, “Surely the darkness will cover me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of the night as if it were a blanket that could conceal him. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: The night would shine like the day
OccurrenceNote: The night, which is dark, is spoken of as if it were bright with light. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: You formed my inner parts
OccurrenceNote: “Inner parts” refers to the interior organs of a person, but here the expression probably stands for the entire body. Alternate translation: “You made my entire body (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: My soul knows this very well
OccurrenceNote: Here “soul” probably refers to the psalmist’s innermost ability to be certain about God’s love and guidance. The translator may, however, treat “soul” here as metonymy for the psalmist’s mind and heart. Alternate translation: “I know this with all my heart” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the depths of the earth
OccurrenceNote: This is probably a way of speaking about a mother’s womb (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: they would be more in number than the sand
OccurrenceNote: This hyperbole means that the writer would be unable to count God’s thoughts. Alternate translation: “there would be more than I could count” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: get away from me, you violent men
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist is only pretending to speak directly to the violent men whom he has in mind. Translators may decide to express this command as a wish. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]])

GLQuote: Do I not hate those, Yahweh, who hate you? Do I not despise those who rise up against you?
OccurrenceNote: These two sentences have similar meanings. The second one strengthens the thought in the first. Both of these questions actually make statements. Alternate translation: “Yahweh, I hate those who hate you! I despise those who rise up against you!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Examine me
OccurrenceNote: This is a request for God to tell the psalmist about any sinful thoughts that he may have. Alternate translation: “Please search me” or “I beg you to search me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Examine me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts
OccurrenceNote: These two sentences have similar meanings. The second one strengthens the thought in the first. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: any wicked way
OccurrenceNote: Here “way” stands for behavior. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the everlasting way
OccurrenceNote: Here “way” refers to trust and obedience in God. Anyone who “walks” this way will have everlasting life. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Their tongues wound like serpents
OccurrenceNote: People who cause conflict by what they say are spoken of as if they had tongues of serpents. Of course, snakes do not do damage with their tongues, but with their bites and especially with poison. Neither can a person make his tongue sharp. Instead, here the idea of a sharp tongue stands for speaking in a way to cause trouble. And the idea the snakes have sharp tongues stands for the fact that many of them have poison. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the hands of the wicked
OccurrenceNote: That is, the power of the wicked (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: have set a trap … have spread a net … have set a snare
OccurrenceNote: The exact kinds of traps are less important than the idea that wicked and proud people are planning to make trouble for the psalmist. If your readers do not know much about different ways of trapping, you may need to reduce this to one line. Alternate translation: “have set a trap to catch me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: listen to my cries
OccurrenceNote: This is a call for help. Alternate translation: “listen to me as I call to you now for help” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: you shield my head in the day of battle
OccurrenceNote: A person’s head is in great danger during battle. Protecting the person’s head represents protecting the whole person. Alternate translation: “you protect me when I go to war” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: battle
OccurrenceNote: Here “battle” probably stands for any kind of severe trouble (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the wicked
OccurrenceNote: The adjective “wicked” can be translated as a noun phrase. Alternate translation: “wicked people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: the mischief of their own lips
OccurrenceNote: The trouble that they themselves caused by what they said. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: cover them
OccurrenceNote: That is, stop them from causing any more trouble. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Let burning coals fall on them; throw them into the fire
OccurrenceNote: Images of fire stand for severe punishment for the wicked. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: men of tongues
OccurrenceNote: those who speak evil of others without cause (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: may evil hunt down the violent man
OccurrenceNote: Here evil is spoken of as if it were someone taking revenge on another person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: he will give justice to the needy
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **justice**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “just.” Alternate translation: “He will act in a just manner to help the needy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: to your name
OccurrenceNote: This represents Yahweh. Alternate translation: “to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: come quickly to me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks as if Yahweh were a person who needed to come from another place to help him. What the psalmist wanted Yahweh to do can be stated clearly. Alternate translation: “come quickly to help me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: May my prayer be like incense
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist asks Yahweh to accept and be pleased with his prayer the way he would accept and be pleased with incense. Alternate translation: “May the my prayer please you the way the sweet smell of incense pleases people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: my prayer
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist wants Yahweh to be pleased with him because he is praying and because of the words of his prayer. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: be like the evening sacrifice
OccurrenceNote: The means to be like the animal that was burned on the altar in the evening. The psalmist speaks as if he wants Yahweh to be as pleased with him as he is with those who bring animals to sacrifice. He wants Yahweh to be pleased because the psalmist is praying or because of the words of his prayer. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: place a guard over my mouth
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks as if evil words were prisoners trying to escape from his mouth. Alternate translation: “please help me not to say things that are evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: guard the door of my lips
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks as if evil words were prisoners trying to escape from his mouth. Alternate translation: “please help me not to say things when I should not” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: hit me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks as if giving a rebuke were physically hitting someone. Alternate translation: “rebuke me” or “hit me so I will listen when he corrects me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: it will be a kindness to me
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **kindness**, you could express the same idea with an adverb. Alternate translation: “he will be acting kindly to me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: it will be like oil on my head
OccurrenceNote: Possible meanings are that the psalmist speaks as if a person correcting him were putting oil on his head: (1) to honor him. Alternate translation: “when he corrects me, I will know that the one who corrects me is doing a good deed to me” or (2) to make his head feel better. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: may my head not refuse to accept it
OccurrenceNote: The head is a synecdoche for the person. The litotes can be translated as a positive statement. Alternate translation: “may I accept it gladly” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]])

GLQuote: my prayer is always against their wicked deeds
OccurrenceNote: The words “wicked deeds” are a metonym for the people who do the wicked deeds. Alternate translation: “I always pray that Yahweh will stop wicked people from doing evil deeds” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Their leaders will be thrown down
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “Someone will throw their leaders down” or (2) “Their leaders will throw them down.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: my eyes are on you
OccurrenceNote: The eyes are a synecdoche for the whole person. Alternate translation: “I am looking to see what you will do” or “I expect you to help me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: in you I take refuge
OccurrenceNote: “I am asking you to protect me” See how “take refuge” is translated in [Psalms 118:9](../118/009.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my soul
OccurrenceNote: The soul is a metonym for the whole person. Alternate translation: “me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: the snares that they have laid for me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of deceiving a good man so the good man will sin or so that the evil people can defeat him as if it were laying a trap for an animal. The word “snares” is a metonym for the people themselves. Alternate translation: “people who are looking for ways to harm me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: from the traps of evildoers
OccurrenceNote: The verb may be supplied from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: “and protect me from the traps that those who do evil have set” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: I cry out for help to Yahweh … I plead for Yahweh’s favor
OccurrenceNote: If these two lines are so much the same that the reader will get the wrong meaning, you can translate them as one line. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: pour out my lament before him … I tell him my troubles
OccurrenceNote: If these two lines are so much the same that the reader will get the wrong meaning, you can translate them as one line. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: pour out my lament before him
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of telling Yahweh why he is sad as if he were pouring all of a liquid out of a container. Alternate translation: “I tell him all about why I am sad” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you know my path
OccurrenceNote: “you know the path I should take.” The psalmist speaks as if what a person does were a path that that person walked along. Alternate translation: “you know the way I should live” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: In the way that I walk they have hidden a trap for me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of people wanting to harm him as if they were trying to trap an animal. Alternate translation: “They are making plans so that whatever I do they can harm me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my life
OccurrenceNote: This is a metonym for “me.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: called out to you
OccurrenceNote: This is a call for help. Alternate translation: “called to you now for help” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: in the land of the living
OccurrenceNote: This idiom refers to a person being alive, as opposed to a person who is dead and in the place of the dead. Alternate translation: “while I am living” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Listen to my call
OccurrenceNote: This is a call for help. See how you translated this in [Psalms 5:1](../005/001.md). Alternate translation: “Listen to me as I call to you now for help” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Bring my soul out of prison
OccurrenceNote: This is a request. The “soul” represents the whole person. Alternate translation: “bring me out of prison” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: give thanks to your name
OccurrenceNote: The word “name” is a metonym for the person. See how you translated this in [Psalms 5:11](../005/011.md). Alternate translation: “give thanks to you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Hear my prayer
OccurrenceNote: The words “my prayer” are a metonym for the person who is praying. See how these words are translated in [Psalms 39:12](../039/012.md). Alternate translation: “Listen to me as I pray to you” or “Be willing to do what I ask you to do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Do not enter into judgment
OccurrenceNote: To “enter into judgment” is an idiom that means to pronounce judgment. Alternate translation: “Please do not judge” or “I beg you not to judge” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: your servant
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of himself as if he were speaking of another person. Alternate translation: “me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: in your sight no one is righteous
OccurrenceNote: Here sight represents judgment or evaluation. Alternate translation: “in your judgment no one is righteous” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: pursued my soul
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “soul” represents the person. Alternate translation: “pursued me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: has crushed me to the ground
OccurrenceNote: Defeating an enemy is spoken of as a heavy object crushing a lighter object on the ground. Alternate translation: “has completely defeated me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: spread my hands out to you
OccurrenceNote: What one does with one’s body here is a metonym for the purpose of doing so. The Israelites would commonly pray while standing with their hands raised and spread out at their sides. Alternate translation: “pray to you with my hands lifted up at my sides” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: my soul thirsts for you in a parched land
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of wanting to be with God as if he were in a parched land and he also was about to die of thirst. Alternate translation: “I want to be with you the way a person in a parched land who is very thirsty wants water” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my soul thirsts for you
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist desires to know Yahweh. The intensity of his desire to know Yahweh is like one who is very thirsty. Alternate translation: “I long for you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my soul
OccurrenceNote: The soul is a metonym for the person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: my spirit faints
OccurrenceNote: Here the “spirit” refers to the whole person. Alternate translation: “I am weak” or “I am very discouraged” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Do not hide your face from me
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of Yahweh refusing to do what the psalmist asks as if Yahweh were refusing to even look at the psalmist. This litotes can be stated as a positive. Alternate translation: “Do not refuse to listen to me” or “Please listen to me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]])

GLQuote: I will become like those who go down into the pit
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “pit” refers to the place of the dead. This phrase is a euphemism for death. Alternate translation: “I will become just another dead person” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: Let me hear your covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: “Cause me to hear of your covenant faithfulness” or “Tell me of your covenant faithfulness.” If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Let me hear of how you are faithful to your covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: the way where I should walk
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of the way people live as if it were a path on which they walk. Alternate translation: “how you want me to live” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: lead me in the land of uprightness
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “help me to live righteously” or (2) “may my life be free of trouble” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the land of uprightness
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) this is a metaphor for righteous living or (2) “a level land,” a metaphor for life free of trouble. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: for your name’s sake
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s name represents his reputation and character. Alternate translation: “because of who you are” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: In your covenant faithfulness cut off my enemies
OccurrenceNote: “Show your covenant faithfulness by cutting off my enemies.” If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “Because you are faithful to your covenant, cut off my enemies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: the enemies of my life
OccurrenceNote: “the enemies of my soul.” My “life” may be understood as representing the speaker. Alternate translation: “my enemies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: my rock
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “the one who keeps me safe” or (2) “the one who gives me strength” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: who trains my hands for war and my fingers for battle
OccurrenceNote: The words “hands” and “fingers” are synecdoches for “me.” If “war” and “battle” are the same word in your language, you can translate this as one line. Alternate translation: “who trains me for war and trains me for battle” or “who trains me for war” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: my covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with anadverb. This could mean: (1) “the one who faithfully loves me” or (2) “the one who faithfully protects me.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: my fortress … take refuge
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist uses many metaphors to emphasize that Yahweh will protect him. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my high tower
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of Yahweh as if he were a fortress that protects him from attack. Yahweh is the one who protects David from harm. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my shield
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of Yahweh as if he were a shield that protects a soldier. Yahweh is the one who protects David from harm. See how this is translated in [Psalms 18:2](../018/002.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the one in whom I take refuge
OccurrenceNote: Going to Yahweh for protection is spoken of as taking refuge in him. Alternate translation: “the one to whom I go so he will protect me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Yahweh, what is man that you take notice of him or the son of man that you think about him?
OccurrenceNote: If your readers would misunderstand these questions, you can express them as statements. Alternate translation: “Man is so small compared to everything else you have made that I am surprised that you take notice of man and that you think about the son of man” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: man … son of man
OccurrenceNote: two words for human beings. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: like a breath … like a passing shadow
OccurrenceNote: The writer compares humans to these thing to emphasize how short their lives are. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: Reach out your hand from above; rescue me out of many waters
OccurrenceNote: David speaks as if God were on land above a flood and had physical hands with which he could pull David out of a flood. The flood is a metaphor for the troubles caused by the “foreigners.” Alternate translation: “You who are able to act, help me overcome my troubles” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: from the hand of foreigners
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to power. Alternate translation: “from the power of foreigners” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Their mouths speak lies
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “mouths” represent the people who speak. Alternate translation: “They speak lies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: their right hand is falsehood
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) David speaks of the custom of raising the right hand to swear that what one is about to say in court is true, “they lie even when they swear to tell the truth,” or (2) the “right hand” is a metaphor for power, “everything they have gotten, they have gotten by telling lies.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: from an evil sword
OccurrenceNote: David speaks of evil people as if they were the swords they use as weapons. Alternate translation: “from evil people who were trying to kill him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: from the hand of foreigners
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to power. See how you translated these words in [Psalms 144:7](./007.md). Alternate translation: “from the power of foreigners” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Their mouths speak lies
OccurrenceNote: The people are represented by their “mouths.” See how you translated these words in [Psalms 144:8](./008.md). Alternate translation: “They speak lies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: their right hand is falsehood
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) David speaks of the custom of raising the right hand to swear that what one is about to say in court is true, “they lie even when they swear to tell the truth,” or (2) the “right hand” is a metaphor for power, “everything they have gotten, they have gotten by telling lies.”See how you translated these words [Psalms 144:8](./008.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: no outcry
OccurrenceNote: Here the outcry is associated with a severe problem that causes the person to cry out. Alternate translation: “no one crying in pain” or “no one crying for help” or “no one calling out for justice” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: bless your name
OccurrenceNote: The word “name” is a metonym for Yahweh himself. See how “may his glorious name be blessed” is translated in [Psalms 72:19](../072/019.md). Alternate translation: “bless you” or “do what makes you happy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: praise your name
OccurrenceNote: The word “name” is a metonym for Yahweh himself. Alternate translation: “praise you” or “tell people how great you are” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: abounding in covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of covenant faithfulness as if it were a physical object of which one could possess a large amount. If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “completely faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: supports all who are falling … raises up all those who are bent over
OccurrenceNote: The psalmist speaks of Yahweh encouraging people as if he were helping people who were physically weak. You may need to translate both lines using only one line. AT “encourages those who are discouraged” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: The eyes of all wait
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “eyes” represents those who watch and wait for Yahweh to act. Alternate translation: “Everyone watches and waits” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: is near to all those who call to him
OccurrenceNote: Here “is near” means “ready to help.” Alternate translation: “is always ready to help all those who call to him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: to all who call to him in trustworthiness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **trustworthiness**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: “to all who tell only the truth when they pray” or “to all whom he trusts when they pray” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: My mouth will speak
OccurrenceNote: Here the words “My mouth” represent the one speaking. Alternate translation: “I will speak” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: let all mankind bless his holy name
OccurrenceNote: The word “name” is a metonym for Yahweh himself. See how “may his glorious name be blessed” is translated in [Psalms 72:19](../072/019.md). Alternate translation: “let all people bless him” or “let all people do what makes him happy” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Praise Yahweh, my soul
OccurrenceNote: Here “soul” represents the writer’s inner being. The writer is commanding his inner being to praise Yahweh. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “I will praise Yahweh with all my soul” or “I give praise to Yahweh with all my life” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: in princes
OccurrenceNote: Here “princes” represents all human leaders. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: in mankind, in whom there is no salvation
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **salvation**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “save.” Alternate translation: “in any person because they cannot save you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: When a person’s life’s breath stops
OccurrenceNote: This is a polite way to refer to someone dying. Alternate translation: When a person dies” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-euphemism]])

GLQuote: he returns to the ground
OccurrenceNote: This means that just as God made the first human, Adam, from the soil, so will a person’s body decay and become soil again when he dies. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Yahweh made heaven and earth
OccurrenceNote: The words “heaven” and “earth” represent everything that exists in the physical universe. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: observes trustworthiness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **trustworthiness**, you could express the same idea with an adjective. Alternate translation: “remains trustworthy” or “remains faithful” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: for the oppressed
OccurrenceNote: This nominal adjective can be stated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “for oppressed people” or “for those whom other people oppress” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: to the hungry
OccurrenceNote: This nominal adjective can be stated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “to hungry people” or “to those who are hungry” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: opens the eyes of the blind
OccurrenceNote: Causing a blind person to see is spoken of as if Yahweh were opening the person’s eyes. Alternate translation: “causes the blind to see” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the blind
OccurrenceNote: This nominal adjective can be stated as adjectives. Alternate translation: “blind people” or “those who are blind” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-nominaladj]])

GLQuote: Yahweh raises up those who are bowed down
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh helping someone is spoken of as if he were physically helping someone to stand up. Alternate translation: “Yahweh helps those who are discouraged” or “Yahweh helps those who are weak” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he lifts up
OccurrenceNote: God helping someone is spoken of as if he were physically lifting them up. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: your God, Zion
OccurrenceNote: Here “Zion” represents all the people of Israel. The writer is speaking to the people of Israel as if they were there listening to him. Alternate translation: “your God, people of Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-apostrophe]])

GLQuote: for all generations
OccurrenceNote: The words “will reign” are understood. Alternate translation: “will reign for all generations” or “will reign forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: it is pleasant
OccurrenceNote: The object may be supplied from the previous phrase. Alternate translation: “it is pleasant to sing praises” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of the people’s sorrow and discouragement as if they were physical wounds, and of Yahweh encouraging them as if he were healing those wounds. Alternate translation: “He encourages those who are sad and helps them to heal from their emotional wounds” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: his understanding cannot be measured
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “no one can measure his understanding” or “his understanding has no limit” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Yahweh lifts up the oppressed
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of Yahweh honoring those who are oppressed as if Yahweh were lifting them up from the ground. Alternate translation: “Yahweh honors the oppressed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: he brings the wicked down to the ground
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of Yahweh humiliating the wicked as if Yahweh were forcing them to lie on the ground. Alternate translation: “he humiliates the wicked” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: to the young ravens when they cry
OccurrenceNote: The verbal phrase can be supplied from the previous line. Alternate translation: “he gives food to the young ravens when they cry” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: the strong legs of a man
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) “strong legs” is a metonym that represents how swiftly a man can run. Alternate translation: “men who can run swiftly” or (2) “strong legs” represents the strength of the whole man. Alternate translation: “how strong a man is” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: who hope in his covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with and adjective. Alternate translation: “who trust him because he is faithful to his covenant” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Jerusalem … Zion
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks to Jerusalem, which he also calls Zion, as if it were a person. The names of the city are metonyms for the people who live in it. Alternate translation: “people of Jerusalem … people of Zion” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: For he strengthens the bars of your gates
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “the bars of your gates” represent the city as a whole. Yahweh will make Jerusalem secure from enemy invasion. Alternate translation: “For he protects Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: he blesses … among you
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of those who live in Jerusalem as if they were Jerusalem’s children. Alternate translation: “he blesses those who live in Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: his command runs very swiftly
OccurrenceNote: The writer describes God’s command as if it were a messenger that moves quickly to deliver God’s message. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: He makes the snow like wool, he scatters the frost like ashes
OccurrenceNote: These emphasize how easy it is for him to do these things. He covers the ground with snow as easily as a person covers something with a wool blanket. And, he removes the frost as easily as the wind blows ashes. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: He dispenses the hail like crumbs
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh scatters hail as easily as a person would scatter bread crumbs. Alternate translation: “He dispenses the hail easily, as if it were crumbs” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: who can withstand the cold he sends?
OccurrenceNote: The writer uses this question to emphasize that it is difficult to endure the cold weather that Yahweh causes. Alternate translation: “no one can live in the cold he sends.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: He sends out his command and melts them
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks of Yahweh’s command as if it were his messenger. The word “command” can be translated with a verb. Alternate translation: “He commands the ice to melt” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: He proclaimed his word to Jacob, his statutes and his righteous decrees to Israel
OccurrenceNote: These two lines mean the same thing and emphasize that Yahweh gave his law only to Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: his statutes and his righteous decrees to Israel
OccurrenceNote: The verbal phrase can be supplied from the previous line. Alternate translation: “He proclaimed his statutes and his righteous decrees to Israel” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: his statutes and his righteous decrees
OccurrenceNote: The words “statutes” and “righteous decrees,” along with “word” in the previous line, all refer to the law of Moses. If your language does not have different words for these terms, you may combine the two lines into one, using either “Jacob” or “Israel” for the people who received them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: Praise Yahweh, you in the heavens … you in the heights
OccurrenceNote: “Praise Yahweh, you in the heavens … you in the sky.” These two lines are parallel, with phrase “the heights” meaning the same thing as “the heavens” in the previous line. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Praise him, sun and moon
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks to the sun and moon as if they were people and commands them to praise Yahweh. Alternate translation: “Praise Yahweh, sun and moon, as people do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: praise him, all you shining stars
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks to the shining stars as if they were people and commands them to praise Yahweh. Alternate translation: “Praise Yahweh, shining stars, as people do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Praise him, highest heaven
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “highest heaven” is an idiom that refers to heaven itself. The writer speaks to heaven as if it were a person and commands it to praise Yahweh. Alternate translation: “Praise Yahweh, highest heaven, as people do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: you waters that are above the sky
OccurrenceNote: The writer speaks to “the waters that are above the sky” as if they are people and commands them to praise Yahweh. The verbal phrase can be supplied from the previous line.
