OccurrenceNote: Eggs of a poisonous snake hatch into more dangerous snakes. “Poisonous snakes” represents evil the people do that harms more and more. Alternate translation: “They make evil that spreads out to make more evil” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: weave a spider’s web
OccurrenceNote: This represents the deeds of the people that are useless. Alternate translation: “produce things and activities that are useless” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Whoever eats of their eggs dies, and if an egg is crushed, it hatches into a poisonous snake
OccurrenceNote: Eating a poisonous egg will kill the one that eats it and represents self-destruction. Breaking the egg allows the young poisonous snake to hatch and represents spreading destruction. Alternate translation: “The activities they do will destroy them and will spread destruction to others” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: if an egg is crushed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “if someone crushes an egg” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Their webs cannot be used for garments, nor can they cover themselves with their works
OccurrenceNote: This means their sinful deeds cannot be covered and hidden, just as a web cannot serve as clothing and cover someone. Alternate translation: “Their evil deeds will be exposed as useless” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Their webs cannot be used for garments
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “They cannot clothe themselves with their webs” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: deeds of violence are in their hands
OccurrenceNote: “Hands” represents the ability and power to do these things and therefore their responsibility. Alternate translation: “they are fully responsible for the violence they do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Their feet run to evil
OccurrenceNote: Here people are represented by their “feet.” This speaks of them doing something quickly as their feet running to it. Alternate translation: “They are quick to do evil things” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: are their roads
OccurrenceNote: “roads” represents their way of life. Alternate translation: “are all they do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: there is no justice in their paths
OccurrenceNote: “paths” represents their way of life. Alternate translation: “they never do what is just” or “everything they do is unjust” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: They have made crooked paths
OccurrenceNote: “Crooked paths” represents the way of life that is corrupt. Alternate translation: “They say and do dishonest things. They are devious” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: justice is far from us
OccurrenceNote: Here “us” refers to Isaiah and the people of Israel. “Far” represents that justice is gone and difficult to get. Alternate translation: “justice is gone and very difficult to get” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclusive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: We wait for light, but see darkness; we look for brightness, but we walk in darkness
OccurrenceNote: Each of these phrases means that the people are waiting for God’s goodness, but it seems like he has abandoned them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: We grope for the wall like the blind … like dead men
OccurrenceNote: This means that because God is not coming to them, they feel helpless, not finding the right path and despairing of the future, with no hope for a vibrant life. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: We growl like bears and moan like doves
OccurrenceNote: These refer to the sounds the people made because they were distressed and mourning. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: our many transgressions
OccurrenceNote: Here “our” refers to Isaiah and the people of Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclusive]])

GLQuote: before you
OccurrenceNote: Here “you” refers to Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-you]])

GLQuote: our sins testify against us
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah describes the sins as a person who goes before God to declare that the people are guilty. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: for our transgressions are with us
OccurrenceNote: “With us” represents being aware of them. Alternate translation: “for we are aware of our transgressions” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Justice is driven back
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “The people drive justice back” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Justice … righteousness … truth … right
OccurrenceNote: These are ideas that Isaiah describes as acting like persons. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Trustworthiness
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah describes this idea as acting like a person. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: Therefore his own arm brought salvation for him
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s “arm” represents his ability and power. Alternate translation: “Yahweh used his own power to save the people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: his righteousness sustained him
OccurrenceNote: “Righteousness” here is a quality that acts like a person. The word can be translated as an adjective. Alternate translation: “he did right as he always would do” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: He put on righteousness as a breastplate and a helmet of salvation upon his head. He clothed himself with garments of vengeance and wore zeal as a mantle
OccurrenceNote: “breastplate,” “helmet,” “garments,” and “mantle” are clothing for war and fighting. Isaiah describes Yahweh as putting these on to punish his people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: fear the name of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Here “name” refers to Yahweh’s reputation and character. Alternate translation: “fear Yahweh” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: from the west … from the sun’s rising
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah combines these words to mean people in all places of the world. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: for he will come as a rushing stream
OccurrenceNote: Narrow valleys in Judah were dry most of the year until a sudden, heavy rain turned them into fast-moving water. When that happened there was a lot of noise and wind. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: driven by the breath of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “which the breath of Yahweh drives” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. Translate as in [Isaiah 30:1](../30/01.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of Yahweh has risen on you
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the glorious things Yahweh has done for the inhabitants of Jerusalem. They are now to show that glory through what they do and say and have hope in the future. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Though darkness will cover the earth, and thick darkness the nations
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases mean the same thing and are combined for emphasis. They refer to “spiritual darkness.” This means all the other people of the world will not know Yahweh or how to please him. This is a metaphor for divine judgment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: yet Yahweh will arise upon you
OccurrenceNote: This means the light of God’s presence will appear for the people of Israel, and it will show the way they should go. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: his glory will be seen on you
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “the people of the nations will see his glory on you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: your daughters will be carried in their arms
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “they will carry your daughters in their arms” or “they will carry your daughters on their hips” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Then you will look and be radiant, and your heart shall rejoice and overflow
OccurrenceNote: These phrases share similar meanings and emphasize that they will be very happy because of what will happen in Jerusalem. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: be poured out to you
OccurrenceNote: This describes that the abundance will be like water that gushes out. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered together to you
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “The people of Kedar will gather their flocks for you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Who are these who fly along like a cloud, and like the doves to their shelters?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses questions and poetic images to draw attention here. He compares the sails of the ships to clouds and doves. This is also a picture of the Israelites returning to the country where they belong. Alternate translation: “Look, I see something like clouds moving quickly and like doves returning to their shelters.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: The coastlands
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the people who live on the coastlands and describes the area of coastlands as if it was people looking out. Alternate translation: “The people from the coastlands” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: they will not be shut day or night
OccurrenceNote: Here “day” and “night” together mean “all the time.” If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “no one will ever shut them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: so that the wealth of the nations may be brought, with their kings being led
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “so that the people of the nations may bring their wealth, along with their kings” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: those nations will be completely destroyed
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “I will completely destroy the people of those nations” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: the place of my feet
OccurrenceNote: This refers to Yahweh’s temple. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: You will also drink the milk of the nations, and will nurse at the breast of kings
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the wealth and plenty that will be drained from foreign nations. Both clauses repeat the same idea for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh will give more valuable building materials to them now. Alternate translation: “instead of wood, I will bring bronze, and instead of stones, I will bring iron” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: I will appoint peace as your governors, and justice your rulers
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh describes “peace” and “justice” as human rulers. This means there will be complete peace and justice in the land of Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Violence will no longer be heard in your land
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “There will no longer be reports of violence in your land” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: but you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise
OccurrenceNote: The physical objects have the names of spiritual qualities. The city of Jerusalem will be a safe place, and the people there will praise Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: for Yahweh will be your everlasting light
OccurrenceNote: Both verses repeat this same idea for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Your sun will no longer set, nor will your moon withdraw and disappear
OccurrenceNote: The moon will not literally disappear. This exaggeration is saying that the light of the sun and the moon will be much less bright than the light of Yahweh. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: the branch of my planting, the work of my hands
OccurrenceNote: These phrases mean approximately the same and are repeated for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the branch of my planting
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh is comparing the people to young shoots coming up that he planted as if he was a gardener. Yahweh has placed his people in the land of Israel. This gives hope to the people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the work of my hands
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh compares the people of Israel to something made by the skill of his handicraft. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: that I may be glorified
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “so that all people may glorify me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison for those who are bound
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean the same thing. They state that God will certainly give freedom to captives. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the year of Yahweh’s favor, the day of vengeance
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases refer to the same span of time. “Year” and “day” are both specific examples that represent the greater whole. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: oil of joy … a mantle of praise
OccurrenceNote: People put oil on themselves and dressed in beautiful, long robes during times of celebration and joy. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: oaks of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: This means Yahweh has caused the people to be strong and sturdy. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: that he may be glorified
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “so that the people’s lives may glorify him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: You will be called
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People will call you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they will rejoice over their share … they will … their land … will be theirs
OccurrenceNote: This still refers to the people of Israel. This can be stated in second person. Alternate translation: “you will rejoice over your share … you will … your land … will be yours” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples
OccurrenceNote: These two clauses mean the same thing. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People from other nations will know their descendants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: their offspring among the peoples
OccurrenceNote: This clause assumes the same verb as the previous one. Alternate translation: “their offspring will be known among the peoples” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-ellipsis]])

GLQuote: clothed me with the garments of salvation; he has clothed me with the robe of righteousness
OccurrenceNote: The people of God speaking as one person now have salvation and righteousness as their distinct appearance visible to all. “Garments” and “robe” are clothing that everyone can see. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: as a bridegroom adorns himself with a turban, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels
OccurrenceNote: This comparison emphasizes that the speaker is extremely happy, joyful, celebrating. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: For as the earth produces its sprouting plants, and as the garden makes its planting grow
OccurrenceNote: This is saying the same thing in two ways. The fact that whatever God says he will do is certainly going to happen is compared to the fact that seeds sprout after planting. Alternate translation: “Just as seeds sown in a garden sprout from the soil and grow” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: righteousness and praise to sprout up
OccurrenceNote: This expression describes these virtues as growing from seed like plants do. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not be quiet
OccurrenceNote: Both of these statements mean the same thing. Here “Zion” and “Jerusalem” both represent the people who live in Jerusalem. Alternate translation: “For the sake of the people of Jerusalem I will not be silent” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: until her righteousness proceeds brightly, and her salvation as a burning torch
OccurrenceNote: Both clauses reassure the people that God will eventually come and save the people of Israel and that it will be as apparent as light is. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: You will also be a crown of beauty in the hand of Yahweh, and a turban of kingship in the hand of your God
OccurrenceNote: These mean the same thing and are combined for emphasis. They say that Jerusalem will become a royal city under the power and authority of God. Yahweh’s hand is a metonym for his power and authority. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: It will no more … will it be said, “Desolate.”
OccurrenceNote: These mean the same thing are combined for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: It will no more be said of you
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “People will no longer say about you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: nor of your land any longer will it be said
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “nor will people any longer say about your land” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: your land will be married
OccurrenceNote: This means Yahweh will love the people of Israel and will always be with them as is a husband. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: as a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you
OccurrenceNote: Here “sons” refers to the people of Israel and “you” refers to Judah, the land of Israel. This means the people will take possession of the land as a man takes possession of his young wife. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, your God will rejoice over you
OccurrenceNote: This emphasizes God’s happiness about his relationship with his people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: watchmen on your walls
OccurrenceNote: This refers to prophets, officials, or possibly angels, who are constantly praying for the people of Jerusalem like watchmen who constantly guard the city. See how you translated “watchmen” in [Isaiah 52:8](../52/08.md) and [Isaiah 56:10](../56/10.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: they are not silent day or night
OccurrenceNote: This means they are continually pleading to Yahweh or calling to each other. Alternate translation: “they are earnestly praying to Yahweh throughout the entire day” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: by his right hand and by the arm of his strength
OccurrenceNote: The right hand and arm represent power and authority. Alternate translation: “by his power and authority” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: I will no longer give your grain as food for your enemies … Foreigners will not drink your new wine
OccurrenceNote: These statements are set together for emphasis and completion. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: those who harvest the grain … those who pick the grapes
OccurrenceNote: These statements are set together for emphasis and completion. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Build it, build the highway
OccurrenceNote: The word “build” is repeated to emphasize that Yahweh urgently wants the road prepared. The “highway” represents the way the people can return. This is similar to [Isaiah 40:3](../40/03.md) and [Isaiah 57:14](../57/14.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Gather out the stones
OccurrenceNote: “Take the stones out of the road to make it smooth.” Stones represent all the obstacles to quick travel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Raise up a signal flag for the nations
OccurrenceNote: A signal flag represents something to draw the attention of others. This means Yahweh is calling the people of the other nations to take notice of the land of Israel and to see what Yahweh has accomplished as he said he would. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the ends of the earth
OccurrenceNote: The places on the earth that are very far away are spoken of as if they were the places where the earth ends. This phrase also forms a merism and refers to everywhere in between the ends. See how you translated this in [Isaiah 40:28](../40/28.md). AT “the farthest places of the earth” or “the entire earth” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: the daughter of Zion
OccurrenceNote: “Daughter” represents the people of Jerusalem (Zion). See how you translated this in [Isaiah 1:8](../01/08.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: See, his reward is with him, and his recompense is going before him
OccurrenceNote: These clauses represent the same idea for emphasis. See how you translated a similar phrase in [Isaiah 40:10](../40/10.md). (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: you will be called
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated actively, “they will call you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Who is this who comes from Edom … Bozrah
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah speaks as a watchman using the question and answer format to present this information about Yahweh’s judgment on Edom, an enemy of Israel. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “I, Yahweh, am coming from Edom, clothed in red from Bozrah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Why are your clothes red, and why … winepress?
OccurrenceNote: If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “The red on your clothing looks makes you look like you have been treading on grapes in a winepress.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: I have trodden grapes
OccurrenceNote: Here “I” refers to Yahweh. This imagery refers to Yahweh destroying his enemies. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the year for my redemption
OccurrenceNote: Here “year” refers to a specific time appointed by Yahweh for restoring Israel. Alternate translation: “the time for my redemption” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: but my own arm
OccurrenceNote: Here “arm” represents power. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: made them drunk in my wrath
OccurrenceNote: This means Yahweh made them stunned and senseless by his full wrath and punishment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I poured out their blood
OccurrenceNote: Here “blood” represents the life of Yahweh’s enemies that was gushing out so they would die. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I will tell of the acts of Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea with a verbal form such as “faithfully” or “faithful.” See how you translated “covenant faithfulness” in [Isaiah 16:5](../16/05.md). Alternate translation: “I will tell about how God has acted faithfully to his covenant” or “I will tell about all the faithful things God has done for his people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: done for us
OccurrenceNote: Here “us” refers to Isaiah and the people of Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-exclusive]])

GLQuote: he lifted them up and carried them
OccurrenceNote: This refers to when God protected and saved the people of Israel from the Egyptians many years earlier. The full meaning of this statement can be made clear. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: who brought them up out of the sea
OccurrenceNote: The story of Yahweh miraculously splitting the waters of the Sea of Reeds so that the Israelites could cross and escape the Egyptians is assumed knowledge. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: the shepherds of his flock
OccurrenceNote: Leaders are sometimes referred to as “shepherds.” Alternate translation: “the leaders of his people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: who made his glorious power go with the right hand of Moses
OccurrenceNote: Here “right hand” represents the power of Yahweh through Moses. This means it was God’s power that enabled Moses to divide the water of the Reed Sea. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Like a horse running on flat land, they did not stumble
OccurrenceNote: This means that the people of Israel were sure-footed as horses in open country on their travels toward Israel from Egypt. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: As the cattle that go down into the valley … rest
OccurrenceNote: This image pictures cattle going into a valley where there is green grass and water and emphasizes that God led the people of Israel and took care of them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: to make yourself a name of praise
OccurrenceNote: Here “name of praise” refers to honor and one’s reputation. Alternate translation: “to make sure you have an honored reputation for yourself” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Where are your zeal and your mighty acts?
OccurrenceNote: The writer uses a question to express deep emotion and concern because it seems God is not helping them. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “We do not see your zeal and your mighty acts!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Your pity and your compassionate actions are kept from us
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “You keep your pity and compassion from us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: though Abraham does not know us, and Israel does not recognize us
OccurrenceNote: These ancestors of the nation of Israel would not able to identify their descendants because they changed so much. “Abraham” and “Israel” represent the people from the distant past. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Yahweh, why do you make us wander from your ways and harden our hearts, so we do not obey you?
OccurrenceNote: Here the writer uses a question to express a complaint of the people to God. If your readers would misunderstand this question, you can express it as a statement. Alternate translation: “Yahweh, you have made us wander from your ways and become stubborn so that we do not obey you.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: why do you make us wander from your ways
OccurrenceNote: To not do what Yahweh commands is spoken of as if a person wanders off of the correct path. Alternate translation: “why do you make do what is wrong” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: harden our hearts
OccurrenceNote: This means to become resistant to Yahweh’s teaching by refusing to listen and obey. Here “heart” represents their motives, feelings and desires. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: who were never called by your name
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The word “name” refers to a family relationship. Alternate translation: “who never belonged to your family” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Oh, if you had
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah introduces this desire for Yahweh’s presence in their past history with a strong exclamation. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: if you had split open the heavens
OccurrenceNote: If Yahweh had shown himself very dramatically by tearing open the sky. The words “split open” refer to ripping a piece of cloth apart. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: mountains would have shaken
OccurrenceNote: The mountains would have trembled as in an earthquake. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: as when fire kindles the brushwood, or the fire makes water boil
OccurrenceNote: This possibly emphasizes how easily God’s presence would have caused the mountains and the people to tremble. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hypo]])

GLQuote: nor eye seen
OccurrenceNote: Here the “eye” refers to the whole person. Alternate translation: “nor has anyone seen” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: call to mind
OccurrenceNote: This is an idiom that means “remember.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: all our righteous deeds are like a menstrual rag
OccurrenceNote: A “menstrual rag” is a cloth that a woman uses during the time of month when she bleeds from her womb. This means all their attempts to please God fail. This sentence was meant to be shocking. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: We have all withered like leaves
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah compares the people of Israel to leaves that dry up when dead. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: our iniquities, like the wind, carry us away
OccurrenceNote: This means their sins, as a community, are the reason for their failure. Isaiah compares the iniquities to the wind as the force for their suffering Yahweh’s punishment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: you have hidden your face from us
OccurrenceNote: This means God gave up on his people and let them suffer. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: in the hand of our iniquities
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “hand” is a metonym for the power of those who are punishing the people for their iniquities. Alternate translation: “as you punish us for our iniquities” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: we are the clay. You are our potter; and we all are the work of your hand
OccurrenceNote: This means God created the people of Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: call to mind
OccurrenceNote: This refers to remembering the past. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: look at us all
OccurrenceNote: Isaiah asks Yahweh to pay attention to their situation. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: Our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised you, has been destroyed by fire
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “The enemy has destroyed our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised you, by fire” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: How can you still hold back, Yahweh? How can you remain silent and continue to humiliate us?
OccurrenceNote: They use questions to express their frustration because God has not yet come to help them. Alternate translation: “Please do not hold back, Yahweh! Please do not remain silent and continue to humiliate us!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: I have spread out my hands all day to a stubborn people
OccurrenceNote: “Spreading out my hands” here is a person’s gesture to show imploring or a strong request. Alternate translation: “I have continually begged a stubborn people to receive my help” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: in gardens … on brick tiles
OccurrenceNote: These refer to Canaanite places for worshiping idols. Their sacred altars were made of bricks, which Yahweh forbid for his altars. Yahweh’s altars were made of stone. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: sit among the graves and keep watch all night
OccurrenceNote: This is a reference to consulting the dead, a practice that Yahweh prohibited. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: eat pork
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh did not allow the people of Israel to eat meat from pigs. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: These things are smoke in my nose
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh compares these people who are continually annoying him to smoke that irritates a person’s breathing. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: a fire that burns all day long
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh compares the people of Israel to a slow-burning fire that sends out smoke without stopping as it irritates. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: into their laps
OccurrenceNote: This means God will punish them to the fullest extent. This expression compares Yahweh punishing the people to dumping on their legs as they are sitting. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: As when juice is found in a cluster of grapes
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh compares the people of Israel to a cluster of grapes that still has some good juice in it. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: when juice is found in a cluster
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated in an active way. Alternate translation: “when you find juice in a cluster” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: I will not ruin them all
OccurrenceNote: This can be expressed positively. Alternate translation: “I will spare some of them who are righteous” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: appoint you for the sword
OccurrenceNote: “The sword” represents various weapons of war that Yahweh will use to punish those who do not respond to Yahweh’s call. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: when I called, you did not answer; when I spoke, you did not listen
OccurrenceNote: Both clauses mean the same and are repeated for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: Look, my servants
OccurrenceNote: “Take notice and pay attention” Yahweh repeats this for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: but you will cry because of the pain of the heart, and will wail because of the crushing of the spirit
OccurrenceNote: These clauses mean the same and the repetition is for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: crushing of the spirit
OccurrenceNote: This expression compares the feeling of terrible disappointment and sorrow to something becoming deformed due to high pressure. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: will be blessed by me, the God of truth
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “I, the God who always speaks the truth, will bless him” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: the former troubles will be forgotten … will be hidden
OccurrenceNote: These clauses can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: “they will forget the former troubles, for these troubles will be out of my memory” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they will be hidden from my eyes
OccurrenceNote: “hidden from my eyes” represents the attention and memory of Yahweh. Alternate translation: “I will not even think about them again” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]])

GLQuote: new heavens and a new earth
OccurrenceNote: Both are extremes that also represent everything between. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-merism]])

GLQuote: the former things will not be remembered or be brought to mind
OccurrenceNote: Both of these clauses mean the same thing and are combined for emphasis. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “you will not even think about what happened in the past” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: But you will be glad
OccurrenceNote: Here “you” refers to all of God’s servants. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-you]])

GLQuote: weeping and cries of distress will no longer be heard in her
OccurrenceNote: You can state this in active form. Alternate translation: “no one will hear weeping and cries of distress any longer in her” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: will be considered a young person
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “people will consider him a young person” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: will be considered cursed
OccurrenceNote: This can be stated this in active form. Alternate translation: “people will consider this person as cursed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: they are the children of those blessed by Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “they are the children of those whom Yahweh blessed” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh compares heaven to a throne and the earth to a footstool to emphasize how great he is. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Where then is the house you will build for me? Where is the place where I may rest?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses questions to emphasize that humans cannot build a place for him to dwell. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: My hand has made all these things
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh is represented by his hand which emphasizes his power and authority. Alternate translation: “I have made all these things” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. Translate as in [Isaiah 30:1](../30/01.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: He who slaughters … also blesses wickedness
OccurrenceNote: These four clauses all describe different ways evil people act and come to the same meaning for emphasis. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: what was evil in my sight
OccurrenceNote: Here sight represents judgment or evaluation. Alternate translation: “what I consider to be evil” or “what is evil in my judgement” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: May Yahweh be glorified
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Glorify Yahweh” or “May Yahweh glorify himself” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: but they will be put to shame
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “but I will put them to shame” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: A sound of battle tumult
OccurrenceNote: The sound represents the real fighting that is going on in the temple as Yahweh is carrying out the punishment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Before she goes into labor, she gives birth; before pain is upon her, she gave birth to a son
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks about Zion as if it were a woman who is about to give birth. Although Zion was destroyed and the people no longer lived there, Yahweh promises that without delay and with little effort an entire nation will come from her. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Will a land be born in one day? Can a nation be established in one moment?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses questions to emphasize how unique this event will be. The series of questions builds tension until Zion is finally mentioned. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Do I bring a baby to the birth opening … born?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses questions to emphasize that he will not fail to fulfill his promises to the people of Jerusalem. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: For you will nurse and be satisfied; with her breasts you will be comforted
OccurrenceNote: This means Jerusalem will be a place of safety and comfort for God’s people. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “For she will satisfy you with her milk; she will comfort you with her breasts” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: like a river … like an overflowing stream
OccurrenceNote: This means God will cause the people of the nations to bring a very large amount of riches, which will be permanent like a river and abundant. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: You will nurse at her side, be carried in her arms, and be dandled on her knees
OccurrenceNote: This means Jerusalem will be a place of safety and comfort for God’s people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: be carried in her arms, and be dandled on her knees
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “she will carry you in her arms and bounce you on her knees with delight” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: so I will comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “so I will comfort you in Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: your bones will sprout
OccurrenceNote: “Bones” refers to the whole body. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: will sprout like the tender grass
OccurrenceNote: “Tender grass” grows fast and strong and compares to the health and vigor of God’s faithful people. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: The hand of Yahweh will be made known to his servants
OccurrenceNote: Here “hand” refers to his power. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will reveal his power to his servants” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: coming with fire
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh’s appearances in the Old Testament are often accompanied by fire that represents Yahweh’s anger and judgment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: like the windstorm
OccurrenceNote: Storms represent Yahweh’s powerful actions to make his judgment effective. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-simile]])

GLQuote: with his sword
OccurrenceNote: “Sword” is one weapon that represents all of warfare and killing. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-synecdoche]])

GLQuote: Those killed by Yahweh will be many
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “Yahweh will kill many people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: enter the gardens
OccurrenceNote: This is a place where people would go to worship idols. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. Translate as in [Isaiah 30:1](../30/01.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: the worms … and the fire
OccurrenceNote: Both clauses describe the same idea to emphasize Yahweh’s punishment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: the worms that eat them
OccurrenceNote: The worms represent the horror of decay and rot that are Yahweh’s punishment on the wicked. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the fire that consumes
OccurrenceNote: Fire also represents Yahweh’s judgment. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: will not be quenched
OccurrenceNote: This can be expressed positively. Alternate translation: “will burn forever” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-litotes]])

GLQuote: all flesh
OccurrenceNote: This expression represents all created living beings that shrink from the dead. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: The word of Yahweh came to him
OccurrenceNote: This idiom is used to announce that God gave messages to him. Alternate translation: “Yahweh gave messages to him” or “Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah
OccurrenceNote: Here “in the days of” is an idiom that refers to the time when a king reigned. Alternate translation: “when Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah
OccurrenceNote: Here “in the days of” is an idiom that refers to the time when a king reigned. Alternate translation: “when Johoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: of Zedekiah
OccurrenceNote: This refers to the rule of Zedekiah. This can be stated explicitly. Alternate translation: “of the reign of Zedekiah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: when the people of Jerusalem were taken away as prisoners
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. It can be stated clearly that they were taken to Babylon. Alternate translation: “when the army of Babylon took the people of Jerusalem away as prisoners” or “when the army of Babylon took the people of Jerusalem as prisoners to Babylon” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: The word of Yahweh came to me, saying
OccurrenceNote: This idiom is used to introduce a special message from God. Alternate translation: “Yahweh gave me a message. He said” or “Yahweh spoke this message to me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: I do not know how to speak
OccurrenceNote: Jeremiah may have been exaggerating to show his fear of speaking in public. Alternate translation: “I do not know how to speak in public” or “I do not know how to make announcements to people” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: Then Yahweh reached out with his hand, touched my mouth
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) this is a metaphor representing Yahweh giving Jeremiah special authority to speak. Alternate translation: “Then it was as though Yahweh touched my mouth” or (2) Jeremiah was seeing a vision and Yahweh actually did this as a symbolic act of giving Jeremiah authority to speak. Alternate translation: “Then Yahweh touched my mouth with his hand” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/translate-symaction]])

GLQuote: I have placed my word in your mouth
OccurrenceNote: This phrase represents giving Jeremiah his message. Alternate translation: “I have given you my message for you to speak to the people” or “I have enabled you to tell the people my message” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: to uproot
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Jeremiah destroying the nations by what he says as if the nations were plants and he were to pull them up out of the ground. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: to destroy and overthrow
OccurrenceNote: Jeremiah uses these words, which mean almost the same thing, to show that this will certainly happen. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-doublet]])

GLQuote: to build and plant
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Jeremiah causing nations to become strong as if they were a building and he would build them, and as if they were plants and he would plant them. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: The word of Yahweh came to me, saying, “What
OccurrenceNote: This idiom is used to introduce a special message from God. See how you translated similar words in [Jeremiah 1:4](./04.md). Alternate translation: “Yahweh gave me a message. He said, ‘What” or “Yahweh spoke this message to me: ‘What” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: I am watching over my word to carry it out
OccurrenceNote: This represents guaranteeing that he will do what he has said. Alternate translation: “I am remembering my word to carry it out” or “I guarantee that I will do what I have said” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: The word of Yahweh came to me a second time, saying
OccurrenceNote: The idiom “The word of Yahweh came to” is used to introduce a special message from God. See how you translated a similar phrase in [Jeremiah 1:4](./04.md), and make any changes as needed. Alternate translation: “Yahweh gave me a message a second time. He said” or “Yahweh spoke this second message to me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: whose surface is churning
OccurrenceNote: The surface refers to the surface of the water in the pot. Jeremiah could see the water boiling. Alternate translation: “whose water is boiling” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Disaster will be opened up out of the north
OccurrenceNote: “Disaster will be let loose from the north.” This represents God causing disaster to come from the north to the south. Alternate translation: “Disaster will come from the north” or “I will send disaster from the north” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: everyone
OccurrenceNote: This generalization refers to the kings of the northern kingdoms. Alternate translation: “every king” or “all of the northern kings” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hyperbole]])

GLQuote: will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) this represents ruling over Jerusalem. Alternate translation: “will rule at the gates of Jerusalem” or (2) this represents judging Jerusalem. Alternate translation: “will judge Jerusalem” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: against all the walls that surround it
OccurrenceNote: Setting their thrones “against all the walls that surround it” represents commanding their armies to destroy the walls surrounding Jerusalem. Alternate translation: “and they will command their armies to destroy the walls surrounding Judah” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: against all the cities of Judah
OccurrenceNote: Setting their thrones “against all the cities of Judah” represents commanding their armies to destroy all the cities of Judah. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: Do not be shattered … I will shatter you
OccurrenceNote: Here “be shattered” represents being extremely afraid, and “shatter” represents causing Jeremiah to be extremely afraid. Alternate translation: “Do not be terrified … I will terrify you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the whole land
OccurrenceNote: Being strong like these things represents being confident and unchanging in saying what God had told him to say. Alternate translation: “I have made you strong against the whole land like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: iron … bronze
OccurrenceNote: These were the strongest materials known at that time. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the whole land
OccurrenceNote: This represents all the people of the land. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in [Jeremiah 1:8](../01/08.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: The word of Yahweh came to me, saying,
OccurrenceNote: This idiom is used to introduce a special message from God. See how you translated similar words in [Jeremiah 1:4](../01/04.md). Alternate translation: “Yahweh gave me a message. He said,” or “Yahweh spoke this message to me:” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: the covenant faithfulness in your youthfulness, your love
OccurrenceNote: The abstract nouns “faithfulness,” “youthfulness” and “love” can be expressed with the adjectives “faithful” and “young,” and the verb “love.” Alternate translation: “how, when you were young, you were faithful to our covenant, and how you loved me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-abstractnouns]])

GLQuote: when we were engaged
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of his relationship with the people of Israel as though they had been engaged to be married. Alternate translation: “when we first agreed that we would marry each other” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the land that was not sown
OccurrenceNote: This can be expressed in active form. Alternate translation: “the land where no one had sown seed” or “the land where no food was growing” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: the firstfruits of his harvest
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Israel as if they were an offering dedicated to God. Alternate translation: “like the firstfruits of his harvest” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: All who ate from the firstfruits were held guilty
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of those who attacked Israel as if they were eating the offering that was set apart for God. Alternate translation: “All who attacked Israel were held guilty like people who ate from the first fruits of his harvest” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: disaster came upon them
OccurrenceNote: The phrase “came upon them” is a metaphor for happened to them. Alternate translation: “Disasters happened to them” or “I made terrible things happen to them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in [Jeremiah 1:8](../01/08.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: house of Jacob, all you clans of the house of Israel
OccurrenceNote: Jacob and Israel were two names for one man, and these two phrases refer to the same group of people. Alternate translation: “all you descendants of Jacob” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: house of Jacob
OccurrenceNote: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to Jacob’s descendants. Alternate translation: “descendants of Jacob” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: the house of Israel
OccurrenceNote: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to Israel’s descendants, who had become the nation of Israel. Alternate translation: “the Israelites” or “the Israelite people group” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: What did your fathers find wrong with me, that they went far from following me? That they went after useless idols and became useless themselves?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses these questions to say that since he has done no wrong, his people should not have rejected him and worshiped idols. Alternate translation: “I did nothing wrong to your forefathers, so they should not have gone far from following me, and they should not have gone after useless idols. By doing that they themselves have become useless!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: they went far from following me
OccurrenceNote: This represents rejecting God and refusing to be loyal to him. Alternate translation: “they rejected me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: they went after useless idols
OccurrenceNote: This represents choosing to be loyal to idols and worship them. Alternate translation: “they worshiped useless idols” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: They did not say
OccurrenceNote: It is implied that they should have said what follows. Alternate translation: “They should have said” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Where is Yahweh, who brought us … Egypt?
OccurrenceNote: This rhetorical question would have been used to show the people’s need of Yahweh. Alternate translation: “We need Yahweh. He is the one who brought us … Egypt.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Where is Yahweh, who led us … lives?
OccurrenceNote: This rhetorical question would have been used to show the people’s need of Yahweh. Alternate translation: “We need Yahweh. He is the one who led us … lives.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: a land of drought and deep darkness
OccurrenceNote: A “land of drought” is a land that does not have enough water. Here “deep darkness” is a metaphor for danger. Alternate translation: “a dangerous land where there is not enough water” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you defiled my land, you made my inheritance an abomination!
OccurrenceNote: These two phrases mean the same thing. Alternate translation: “you sinned and made the land I gave you disgusting to me!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: you defiled my land
OccurrenceNote: Here “defiled” represents making the land unacceptable to God. They did this by sinning against him there when they worshiped idols. Alternate translation: “by sinning, you made my land no good” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: my inheritance
OccurrenceNote: This could mean: (1) God is speaking of his land as if he had inherited it. Alternate translation: “my land” or (2) God is speaking of the land he gave to Israel as if he had given it to them as an inheritance. Alternate translation: “the land I gave you” or “the land I gave you as an inheritance” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Where is Yahweh?
OccurrenceNote: This question would have shown that they wanted to obey Yahweh. Alternate translation: “We need to obey Yahweh!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: The shepherds transgressed against me
OccurrenceNote: The leaders are spoken of as if they were shepherds and the people who followed them were sheep. Alternate translation: “Their leaders sinned against me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: walked after unprofitable things
OccurrenceNote: Here “walked after” represents obeying or worshiping. Alternate translation: “obeyed unprofitable things” or “worshiped unprofitable things” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Has a nation exchanged gods … gods?
OccurrenceNote: God uses this question to tell the people of Israel that other nations continue to worship their own gods. They do not change and worship other gods. Alternate translation: “You will see that no nation has ever exchanged gods … gods.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: But my people have exchanged their glory for what cannot help them
OccurrenceNote: Here God speaks as though he were not speaking directly to his people. Alternate translation: “But you, my people, have exchanged me, your glorious God, for what cannot help you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: their glory
OccurrenceNote: This expression refers to God himself, who is glorious. Alternate translation: “their glorious God” or “me, your glorious God” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: for what cannot help
OccurrenceNote: Here false gods are spoken of in terms of what they cannot do. Alternate translation: “for false gods, which cannot help” or “for gods who cannot help” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in [Jeremiah 1:8](../01/08.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: have abandoned the springs of living waters
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of himself as if he were springs of living waters. Alternate translation: “have abandoned me, their springs of living waters” or “have abandoned me, who is like springs of living water” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: have dug out cisterns for themselves
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of false gods as if they were cisterns that people dig in order to get water. Alternate translation: “have gone to false gods, which are like cisterns they have dug for themselves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Is Israel a slave? Was he born in his master’s home? So why has he become plunder?
OccurrenceNote: Though Yahweh was speaking to the people of Israel, he used the third person as though he were talking to someone else about Israel. Alternate translation: “Israel, are you a slave? Were you born at home? So why have you become plunder?” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: Is Israel a slave? Was he born in his master’s home?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses these questions to tell why Israel should not have become plunder. Alternate translation: “Israel is not a slave. Israel was not born at home.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: Was he born in his master’s home
OccurrenceNote: Here “born in his master’s home” is metonym for being born into slavery. Alternate translation: “Was he born a slave” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: So why has he become plunder?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses this question to indicate that Israel should not have become plunder. Alternate translation: “So he should not have become plunder.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: So why has he become plunder
OccurrenceNote: Here “become plunder” represents being attacked and taken as captives to another country. Alternate translation: “So why has Israel been taken away as captives” or “So why have Israel’s enemies taken Israel away as captives” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Young lions roared against him. They made a lot of noise
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Israel’s enemies attacking Israel as if the enemies were lions roaring and attacking Israel. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: made his land a horror
OccurrenceNote: This represents destroying the land in such a way that people will feel horror when they see it. Alternate translation: “destroyed Israel’s land” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: His cities are destroyed without any inhabitants
OccurrenceNote: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “They have destroyed Israel’s cities and now no one lives in them” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: Did you not do this to yourselves when you abandoned Yahweh your God, while he was leading you along the way?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses this question to remind Israel that it is their own fault that their enemies attacked them. Alternate translation: “You caused this yourselves by abandoning Yahweh your God while he was leading you along the way.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: So now, why take the road to Egypt and drink the waters of Shihor? Why take the road to Assyria and drink the waters of the Euphrates River?
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh uses these questions to remind his people that it does not do any good to ask Egypt and Assyria to help them. Alternate translation: “It does not help you to go to Egypt and drink from the waters of the Shihor River, or to go to Assyria and drink from the waters of the Euphrates River.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: why take the road to Egypt and drink the waters of Shihor … Why take the road to Assyria and drink the waters of the Euphrates River
OccurrenceNote: These are a metaphor for asking the Egyptian and Assyrian armies to help them. Alternate translation: “why ask the Egyptians to help you … Why ask the Assyrians to help you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Your wickedness rebukes you, and your faithlessness punishes you
OccurrenceNote: Both of these phrases mean that their punishment is the result of their wicked behavior. Alternate translation: “Because you have been wicked and unfaithful, I will punish you” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-personification]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-parallelism]])

GLQuote: it is wicked and bitter
OccurrenceNote: Here the word “bitter” describes “wicked.” Alternate translation: “it is bitterly wicked” or “it is extremely wicked” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-hendiadys]])

GLQuote: For I broke your yoke that you had in ancient days; I tore your fetters off you. Still you said, ‘I will not serve!’
OccurrenceNote: Here “broke your yoke” and “tore your fetters off you” are metaphors for setting them free from slavery. The people of Israel had been slaves in Egypt. Alternate translation: “Long ago I released you from slavery, but still you refused to worship me!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: since you bowed down on every high hill and beneath every leafy tree, you adulterer
OccurrenceNote: What they bowed down to can be stated clearly. Here “adulterer” is a metaphor for someone who is unfaithful to God. Alternate translation: “You bowed down to idols and worshiped them instead of me, like an adulterous wife who is unfaithful to her husband” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: I planted you as a choice vine, completely from pure seed
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of making his people into a great nation in Canaan as if they were the seed of a grapevine that he had planted. Alternate translation: “I, Yahweh, started you with a very good beginning, like a farmer who uses excellent seed to plant the best kind of vine” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: How then have you have changed yourself into a corrupt, worthless vine?
OccurrenceNote: God uses this question to rebuke his people for changing and becoming like a corrupt worthless vine. Alternate translation: “But you have changed yourself into a corrupt, worthless vine!” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: this is the declaration of the Lord Yahweh
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated a similar phrase in [Jeremiah 1:8](../01/08.md). Alternate translation: “this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: How can you say, ‘I … have not walked after the Baals’?
OccurrenceNote: God uses this question to rebuke his people for saying that they have not worshiped the Baals. Alternate translation: “You lie when you say, ‘I … have not walked after the Baals.’ (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: walked after
OccurrenceNote: This is a metaphor for serving or worshiping. (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: you are a swift female camel running here and there
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Israel worshiping other gods as if they were like a female camel running in different directions looking for a male camel to mate with. Alternate translation: “You are like a swift female camel running back and forth looking for a male camel to mate with” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: a wild donkey accustomed to the wilderness, in her heat sniffing the wind
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Israel worshiping other gods as if they were a wild female donkey running to find male donkeys. Alternate translation: “You are like a young female donkey that lives in the desert. When she wants to mate she is out of control and constantly sniffs the breeze to find a mate” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: in her heat
OccurrenceNote: This phrase is an idiom referring to the time when a female donkey wants to mate with male donkeys. Alternate translation: “when she wants to mate” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]])

GLQuote: Who can restrain her lust?
OccurrenceNote: This question is used to emphasize that no one can control a female donkey when she is wants to mate with a male donkey. Alternate translation: “No one can turn her around when she wants to mate.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]])

GLQuote: You must restrain your feet from becoming bare and your throat from being thirsty!
OccurrenceNote: God speaks of Israel wanting to worship other gods as if they were running around in the desert looking for those gods. Alternate translation: “I have told you to stop running here and there chasing after false gods, because all that it does is wear out your sandals and make you very thirsty” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: It is hopeless
OccurrenceNote: “There is no hope for us to restrain ourselves.” This implies that they cannot stop themselves from running after other gods. Alternate translation: “We cannot stop ourselves” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: No, I love strangers and go after them!
OccurrenceNote: Here “strangers” represents foreign gods, and “go after them” represents worshiping them. Alternate translation: “We must follow after foreign gods and worship them!’” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: the house of Israel
OccurrenceNote: The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house. In this case it refers to Israel’s descendants. See how you translated this in [Jeremiah 2:4](../02/04.md). Alternate translation: “the Israelites” or “the Israelite people group” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: when he is found
OccurrenceNote: This idiom means that someone discovers that the person’s actions. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: “when someone finds him” or “when people know that he has stolen things” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-idiom]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-activepassive]])

GLQuote: These are the ones who say to the tree, ‘You are my father,’ and to the stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’
OccurrenceNote: Here “tree” and “stone” represent idols carved from wood and stone. These words emphasize that the idol was made of ordinary things and is not worthy of worship. Alternate translation: “These people are the ones who say to a carved piece of wood, ‘You are my father,’ and to a carved stone, ‘You gave birth to me.’” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metonymy]])

GLQuote: their back faces me and not their faces
OccurrenceNote: “their backs are toward me; their faces are not toward me.” This represents them rejecting God. Alternate translation: “they have turned away from me” or “they have turned their backs toward me and not their faces” or “they have completely rejected me” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-metaphor]])

GLQuote: Arise and save us
OccurrenceNote: It can be made clear that they say this to Yahweh. “Yahweh, come and save us” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-explicit]])

GLQuote: Yet where are the gods that you made for yourselves?
OccurrenceNote: With this question God implies that people should ask the gods they worship to help them. He uses this irony to show that he is angry that they worship other gods. Alternate translation: “You should ask the gods you made to help you.” or “You do not ask the gods you made to help you.” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-rquestion]] and [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-irony]])

GLQuote: Let them arise if they wish to save you in your time of troubles
OccurrenceNote: God implies that false gods should help the people who worship them. He knows that false gods cannot help people. When he said this he was using irony to show that he was angry that his people worshiped false gods. Alternate translation: “You do not ask them because know you that they cannot save you in your time of troubles” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-irony]])

GLQuote: this is Yahweh’s declaration
OccurrenceNote: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in [Jeremiah 1:8](../01/08.md). Alternate translation: “this is what Yahweh has declared” or “this is what I, Yahweh, have declared” (See: [[rc://en/ta/man/translate/figs-123person]])

GLQuote: They would not accept discipline
